questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your invoice-extraction system reports 96% accuracy in aggregate. Customer complaints concentrate on credit memos and refund-only invoices. What measurement change would have caught this before customers did?
options: Raise the overall accuracy bar from 96% to 99%
Increase aggregate sample size
Stratify accuracy by document subtype and key field so segment-level performance (e.g., 99% on standard invoices, 71% on credit memos) is visible and aggregate numbers can't hide local failures
Add more validation rules
questions.rationale: Aggregate metrics hide local failure. Stratified sampling and per-segment accuracy reveal exactly which subtypes are underperforming. Raising the global bar doesn't help when the bad segments are dominated by good ones.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your document-extraction agent returns a self-rated confidence of 0.92 on nearly every output, regardless of input quality. Leadership wants to use this score to skip human review on 'high-confidence' results. What's the prerequisite discipline?
options: Trust the 0.92 threshold and start skipping review immediately
Lower the routing threshold to 0.85 to be safe

Calibrate the self-reported scores against a labeled validation set — map model confidence to actual accuracy per document type and field, then defend any routing threshold from that mapping (e.g., '0.85 raw confidence corresponds to 91% actual accuracy on invoice headers')
Apply a single universal threshold across all document types
questions.rationale: Raw self-reported confidence is uncalibrated and often miscalibrated. Mapping it to actual accuracy on a labeled set turns it into a defensible routing signal. Without that, any threshold is theatre.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two reputable sources in your research synthesis cite different figures for global semiconductor capacity. The synthesizer flags this as a contradiction. Investigation shows the sources are from different quarters. What structural change prevents the false-contradiction pattern in future?
options: Pick the more recent source automatically

Have subagents include data-collection or publication dates as required metadata on every claim, so the coordinator can recognize temporal evolution and present it as a time series rather than a contradiction
Use only one source per topic
Have an LLM judge reconcile contradictions case by case
questions.rationale: Many 'contradictions' are temporal differences. Date metadata at the claim level lets the coordinator distinguish 'A says X in March, B says Y in October' from 'A and B genuinely disagree.' Without dates, that distinction is unreachable.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your research reports flatten everything into prose: a comparison of five vendor prices, a regulatory timeline, and a list of technical limitations all read as paragraphs. Readers complain that finding specific facts is slow. What's the discipline?
options: Make the prose more detailed
Render content according to its shape: tabular comparisons as tables, timelines as ordered lists, and narrative passages as prose — uniform formatting destroys structural signal
Add more section headings to the prose
Use bullet points for everything
questions.rationale: Content-type-appropriate rendering is the named Domain 5.6 skill. Tables for comparisons, prose for narrative, lists for enumerations. Flattening everything to prose hides exactly the structure readers need.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your healthcare client requires Zero Data Retention. Your team proposes moving the overnight chart-summarization workload to the Message Batches API for cost savings. Why can't you?
options: Batch API doesn't support summarization tasks
Batch API is not eligible for Zero Data Retention; ZDR workloads must use the synchronous API even when latency wouldn't otherwise demand it. Prompt Caching remains available as a cost optimization
Batch API would expose PHI in custom_id strings
Batch API charges extra for healthcare workloads
questions.rationale: ZDR ineligibility for Batch API is a named exam fact. When ZDR is required, synchronous is the only path even for non-blocking workloads. The cost lever that remains is Prompt Caching.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your research subagent failed to fetch three of seven planned sources. The synthesis agent writes a report using only the four that succeeded and presents it as complete. A reviewer later catches the omission. What discipline should the synthesizer have applied?
options: The synthesizer should retry the failed sources until they succeed
Gap declaration: the report should state explicitly which sources failed, why, and what the analysis therefore could not address — silent omission misrepresents the coverage of the work
The synthesizer should pad the report with related sources to compensate
The coordinator should hide the failure from the user to maintain trust
questions.rationale: The named rule is that reports declare gaps explicitly rather than omitting them. Silent omission is the canonical failure of multi-agent research systems; transparent gap declaration is the discipline that earns trust.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your 12-step compliance audit pipeline runs roughly two hours end-to-end. Yesterday it crashed at step 9 due to a transient cloud issue, and the team had to re-run the whole pipeline from scratch this morning, losing the work of the first eight steps. Which pattern provides durability?
options: Add an exponential-backoff retry inside each step

Persist each step's output to a known location and record completion in a manifest the coordinator reads on startup; on resume, completed steps are skipped, and execution continues from the first incomplete step
Increase the timeout on every step
Run on a machine with more memory
questions.rationale: Crash-recovery manifests are the named pattern for durable multi-step pipelines. Without them, every crash restarts from zero. The manifest is structured state on disk; retries and timeouts treat symptoms, not the durability gap.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Inside an agent loop, what field on the API response should drive the decision to call another tool versus return to the user?
options: The presence of any text in content[0].text
The stop_reason field on the response object
A boolean is_complete flag on the assistant message
Whether the response includes a finish_turn block
questions.rationale: stop_reason is the structured signal: tool_use means run the requested tool and continue; end_turn means stop. The other options describe fields that do not exist or are not reliable termination signals.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your coordinator's running history says 'all citations must be peer-reviewed.' A literature subagent spawned later returns blog posts. Most likely cause?
options: The subagent ignored the rule and needs prompt tuning
The model used by the subagent has weaker instruction-following
The constraint never reached the subagent's task payload
The subagent's tool descriptions allowed non-academic sources
questions.rationale: Subagents start with empty context. Whatever exists in the coordinator's conversation history is invisible unless explicitly bundled in the Task payload. The other options blame the wrong layer.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An architect proposes letting subagents call each other directly to skip a coordinator hop. What is the principal cost of this change?
options: Higher per-call token usage for the routing prompts
Loss of central observability and policy enforcement
Incompatibility with the Claude Agent SDK Task tool
Reduced parallelism across waves
questions.rationale: Hub-and-spoke's value is architectural control: one chokepoint for visibility, recovery, and policy. Peer-to-peer subagent calls sacrifice that. Token cost, SDK compatibility, and parallelism aren't impaired.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Onboarding steps are: (1) fetch HR profile, (2) provision email, (3) provision Slack, (4) provision GitHub, (5) compile welcome packet. Steps 2-4 are independent. Most cost-effective change?
options: Merge 2-4 into a single 'provision_all' tool
Cache the HR profile to make step 1 faster
Move the whole flow to the Message Batches API
Emit Task calls for 2-4 in one coordinator turn
questions.rationale: Independent steps in the same phase belong in one parallel wave. Merging tools loses specialization; caching helps a different step; Batch API is for non-interactive workloads.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your medical-records agent must redact PHI before any outbound email. The rule lives in the system prompt and is skipped under ~2% of long sessions. Most reliable fix?
options: Inject the rule into a user message every turn
Use a PreToolUse hook on the email tool to enforce it
Move to a model with stronger instruction-following
Add a post-send audit that flags violations
questions.rationale: Prompt-level rules degrade under context pressure. A PreToolUse hook makes the bad sequence structurally unreachable. The other options are still probabilistic or only detect violations after the fact.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 4-hour regulatory pipeline crashed at step 14 of 18 and had to restart from step 1. Which pattern best prevents this category of waste?
options: Exponential backoff retries inside each step
Move the pipeline to the Message Batches API
A manifest of completed steps and persisted outputs
Reduce step count by combining adjacent validators
questions.rationale: Crash-recovery manifests are the canonical pattern: each step persists its output and completion status, and resume logic skips completed steps. Retries can't recover from a process crash; Batch API isn't a control-flow tool.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator analyzing 'the state of small modular reactors' split work into four vendor-focused subagents. The final report covers vendors well but misses regulation, fuel, and grid integration. Where is the bug?
options: The synthesis subagent dropped material between input and output
The vendor subagents each performed below expectations
The coordinator's partition was too narrow for the question
The coordinator should have spawned more vendor subagents
questions.rationale: Granularity is a coordinator decision. Splitting by vendor structurally precludes coverage of cross-cutting dimensions. The subagents executed their assigned scope; the partition was the bug.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An agent escalated a refund within standard policy because the message had exclamation marks and the word 'ridiculous.' What does this expose?
options: Escalation logic is conflating sentiment with operational triggers
The model is too conservative and needs aggressiveness tuning
All refund decisions should require human approval
The system needs a dedicated sentiment-analyzer tool
questions.rationale: Escalation triggers must be operational: policy gaps, explicit human requests, inability to proceed. Customer tone is not a trigger when the path forward is clear.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: DAG: collect_raw and review_lit have no deps. clean_data depends on collect_raw. stats_analysis depends on clean_data and review_lit. write_report depends on stats_analysis. How many waves?
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.rationale: Wave 1: collect_raw + review_lit. Wave 2: clean_data. Wave 3: stats_analysis. Wave 4: write_report. The longest dependency chain determines wave count, not node count.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An agent's conversation history is near the context limit. The team plans to evict the oldest turns each round. What is the main risk this introduces?
options: Cache invalidation makes API calls noticeably slower
It evicts arbitrary facts the agent may still need later
It forces the system prompt to be recomputed each turn
Newer models handle truncation poorly versus older ones
questions.rationale: Naive truncation is information-blind: it removes by position, not relevance. Verified IDs, prior commitments, or escalation history can disappear silently. Structured summarization plus a persistent facts block is the disciplined alternative.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team consolidates four customer-facing agents into one with all 18 of their tools. The lead engineer thinks this is simpler. What is the expected production effect?
options: Latency improves because one delegation hop is skipped
Tool-selection accuracy degrades past the 5-8 tool range
Token cost drops because routing prompts are removed
Reliability improves because there's a single failure point
questions.rationale: The super-agent anti-pattern: past ~8 tools, attention fragments and selection accuracy falls regardless of description quality. Specialized subagents with 4-6 tools each, coordinated by a hub, is the recommended shape.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A user writes: 'hold my next delivery, refund Tuesday's duplicate, change my contact to email.' The agent only handles the delivery hold. Right structural change?
options: Ask the user to resend each concern separately
Process concerns serially with intermediate confirmations
Switch to a model with a larger input context
Decompose, share context, fan out, then synthesize one reply
questions.rationale: Multi-concern decomposition: identify each concern, fetch shared context once, fan out on independent work, return a unified response. The other options either degrade UX or duplicate lookups.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Three parallel subagents run. Two return clean results; the third hits a credentials error. Correct hub-and-spoke behavior?
options: Discard the two successes and restart the whole wave
Have the successful spokes retry on the third's behalf
Coordinator decides whether to retry, degrade, or report a gap
Abort the entire request because partials are unsafe
questions.rationale: Each spoke fails or succeeds independently. The coordinator owns the decision about what partial completion means: retry, degrade, or surface the gap. Siblings do not retry for each other.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two hours into a Claude Code session, the agent uses generic naming instead of the specific patterns it followed earlier, and re-reads files it already opened. What is happening?
options: The CLAUDE.md file was silently unloaded mid-session
Mid-session model downgrade requires a restart
Context degradation; mitigate with scratchpad + /compact
max_tokens is too low and responses are truncating early
questions.rationale: 'Reverting to generic patterns' and 'forgetting earlier specifics' are the textbook symptoms of context degradation. Persistent scratchpads anchor load-bearing facts; /compact reclaims attention from low-signal noise.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An engineer wants live customer chat to run through the Message Batches API to save 50%. Why is this fundamentally wrong?
options: Batch API charges a premium when tools are involved
Batch results can take up to 24 hours; users are waiting
Batch API does not support any form of tool calling
Batch jobs can't be combined with system prompts
questions.rationale: Batch trades latency for cost: results may take up to 24 hours. Interactive workloads are incompatible. Batch fits non-blocking back-office processing.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your multi-agent system's first synthesis is reliably ~80% complete. The remaining gaps could be closed with targeted re-queries. Current design ships the first synthesis directly. What is missing?
options: A larger context window on the synthesis agent
A coordinator gap-evaluation step that re-delegates targeted queries
Self-scored confidence on the synthesis output
Two synthesis agents running in parallel and averaged
questions.rationale: Iterative refinement at the coordinator level is the named pattern. The coordinator inspects for gaps and re-delegates. Self-scored confidence is uncalibrated; averaging duplicates doesn't close coverage gaps.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: get_invoice_pdf(invoice_id) returns a specific PDF when called. A 'compliance template library' is a static set of 50 documents agents read before drafting. Classify each.
options: Both are Tools because both return data
get_invoice_pdf is a Tool; the template library is a Resource
get_invoice_pdf is a Resource; the template library is a Tool
Both are Resources because both produce content
questions.rationale: Tools execute and return computed results from inputs. Resources are addressable static content the agent reads. 'Retrieval that runs and returns' is a tool; 'a catalog the agent browses' is a resource.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: search_help_articles and search_internal_wiki have similar descriptions. The agent picks the wrong one ~30% of the time. Most effective first fix?
options: Add a routing classifier upstream of the agent
Combine them into one tool with a 'source' parameter
Add a system-prompt rule mapping keywords to tools
Rewrite both descriptions with explicit negative bounds
questions.rationale: Tool descriptions are the primary input to selection. Semantic overlap causes misrouting; negative bounds ('does NOT search internal wiki') eliminate it. Combining loses specialization; classifiers and prompt rules treat the symptom.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your fetch_supplier_record tool returns just the string 'error' on failure. Coordinator can't distinguish a malformed ID, a transient outage, or a permission denial. What's missing?
options: Internal retry-with-backoff before failing
A circuit breaker after N consecutive failures
Structured error metadata: category, retryable, detail
Longer client-side timeouts on every call
questions.rationale: Opaque errors force blind retries. Categorized errors let the coordinator distinguish 'fix the input' from 'try again later' from 'you can't do this' deterministically.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer committed a literal personal Notion token in .mcp.json to a public repo. The right corrective action?
options: Add .mcp.json to .gitignore and leave the commit alone
Restrict the token's scope in Notion and re-commit it
Replace the literal with a placeholder and re-commit
Rotate the token; use env-var expansion or ~/.claude.json
questions.rationale: Project .mcp.json is committed; secrets there are exposed in history. Rotate first (gitignore doesn't undo history), then keep the shape committed with ${ENV_VAR} or move personal config to ~/.claude.json.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: You need to guarantee that extract_metadata runs first on every uploaded document. Which tool_choice setting forces it?
options: tool_choice: 'auto' plus a system-prompt instruction
tool_choice: 'any' so the model is forced to call something
tool_choice: {type: 'tool', name: 'extract_metadata'}
tool_choice: 'required' with a few-shot example
questions.rationale: Only the named-tool form guarantees a specific tool runs. 'any' forces some tool but lets the model pick; 'auto' is discretionary; 'required' isn't a documented value of this field.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A do_data_thing tool is being invoked with images, CSVs, and natural-language questions, working unpredictably. Clean fix?
options: Rename it to handle_data so it's treated as fallback
Add input validation that rejects unknown types
Decompose into purpose-specific tools with contracts
Write a much more detailed tool description
questions.rationale: Generic tools invite generic — and wrong — usage. Structural decomposition with explicit contracts and negative bounds is the fix. Validation only catches misuse after it's attempted.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A search_orders tool returns the same error code for 'zero matches' and 'service offline.' The agent retries both. Which discipline is missing?
options: The agent should try a fallback search first
The tool should never return zero results
The tool should distinguish empty success from access failure
The agent should call the tool twice and compare results
questions.rationale: Empty results are successful queries with no hits; access failures are failed queries. Conflating them wastes retries on empty queries or hides real outages.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A single agent has 16 tools (inventory, orders, returns mixed). Tool-selection accuracy dropped from 92% to 70%. Best structural fix?
options: Rewrite every description with much more detail
Decompose into three specialized subagents under a hub
Add a router tool the agent calls first
Remove the four least-used tools from the agent
questions.rationale: Past ~8 tools, attention fragments regardless of description quality. The structural fix is specialization: smaller per-agent tool sets coordinated centrally.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your data agent wastes 4-6 calls per session running introspection to learn the warehouse schema. Which MCP primitive solves this?
options: A Tool called describe_schema run on every session
A Prompt template that hard-codes the schema
A Resource exposing the schema catalog as static content
A larger model that guesses schemas more accurately
questions.rationale: Catalogs are Resources. Agents read them as context; they don't execute them. Replacing exploratory tool calls with a readable catalog is the canonical Resource use case.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A subagent gets transient 503s on ~7% of calls; the coordinator escalates each one to humans. Which discipline correctly assigns recovery responsibility?
options: Always escalate every failure for central visibility
Have the coordinator perform retries for the subagent
Suppress 503s silently and continue with empty results
Retry transient failures locally; escalate only what cannot resolve
questions.rationale: Errors should be handled at the lowest level capable of resolving them. Transient → local retry. Unresolvable → escalate with attempt history and partial results.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two third-party MCP tools return dates in ISO-8601 and Unix epoch respectively. The agent occasionally compares them as strings and gets wrong orderings. Best architectural fix?
options: Add a prompt instruction warning about date formats
Normalize formats at the MCP-server adapter layer
Add a third tool that converts between formats
Lower temperature so fewer mistakes happen
questions.rationale: Prompt cautions are probabilistic. Adapter-layer normalization makes the failure mode structurally impossible because the agent only ever sees one format.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team rule lives in one senior dev's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. New contractors don't get it. Where should the rule actually live?
options: In the senior dev's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (status quo)
In a README.md that contractors are told to read
In ~/.claude/skills/ as an on-demand Skill
In the project's committed .claude/CLAUDE.md
questions.rationale: Project-level CLAUDE.md is the home for team-wide rules: committed, auto-loaded for anyone who clones. User-level CLAUDE.md is private and never reaches teammates.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: You want Terraform style rules to apply only when editing .tf files, regardless of which directory they live in. Best configuration?
options: Put the Terraform rules in the root CLAUDE.md
Add a CLAUDE.md to every dir that contains .tf files
A Skill at /terraform-style invoked manually before editing
.claude/rules/terraform.md with paths: ['**/*.tf']
questions.rationale: .claude/rules/ with glob frontmatter is built for file-type-scoped conventions across directories. Root CLAUDE.md inflates every conversation; per-directory files don't scale; manual invocation is unreliable.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Starting from default permission mode in Claude Code, how many Shift+Tab presses reach plan mode?
options: One press
Two presses (default → acceptEdits → plan)
Three presses (default → acceptEdits → readOnly → plan)
Plan mode is not reachable via Shift+Tab
questions.rationale: The cycle is default → acceptEdits → plan. Two presses from default reaches plan. Auto mode is a separate opt-in not in the default cycle.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Mid-refactor, your main Claude Code session's context is being eaten by grep dumps and file reads from exploration. The refactor itself is stalling. Best move?
options: Restart the session and re-explain the refactor
Switch the main session into plan mode
Increase max_tokens so the model can write more
Use the Explore subagent for further discovery
questions.rationale: Explore is purpose-built for offloading noisy discovery: read-only, Haiku by default, returns a summary. Plan mode keeps the noise in the main session; restarts lose the in-flight work.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A /publish-release Skill must (1) require a --tag argument, (2) not pollute the parent context, (3) be restricted to git, gh, and Write tools. Which frontmatter combination?
options: argument-hint, context: fork, allowed-tools
disable-model-invocation: true, paths: [...]
context: shared, auto-approve: true
argument-hint, model: haiku, read-only: true
questions.rationale: Each concern maps to a distinct frontmatter field: argument-hint forces the parameter at autocomplete, context: fork isolates execution, allowed-tools whitelists the tool surface.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A project Skill at .claude/skills/test-fixture/SKILL.md exists. You add a same-named personal variant at ~/.claude/skills/test-fixture/SKILL.md. Your variant never runs. Why?
options: Skills only load from project directories
~/.claude/skills/ is reserved for Anthropic built-ins
Same-named Skills in different locations merge together
Project Skills take precedence over personal Skills with the same name
questions.rationale: Same-name collisions resolve in favor of the project Skill. Use a different name for your personal variant so both coexist.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: `claude "audit this PR"` hangs in GitHub Actions but works on a laptop. Minimal change?
options: Add the `-p` flag
Add a `--timeout` flag
Run the step under a pseudo-TTY
Switch to a smaller, faster model
questions.rationale: Without -p, Claude Code starts interactive and waits for user input. CI has no interactive input, so it hangs. -p is the canonical non-interactive flag.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your Dockerized CI behaves inconsistently because each developer's local hooks, Skills, and CLAUDE.md files leak into auto-discovery. Which flag fixes it?
options: --clean
--bare
--isolated
--no-config
questions.rationale: --bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, Skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md. It's the Anthropic-recommended CI flag and is slated to become the default for -p.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your CI parses Claude Code review output with regex and breaks ~1 in 8 runs. You need JSON with file, line, severity, fix. Where does schema-validated content appear with --output-format json --json-schema?
options: In response.result (the natural-language field)
In response.content[0].text
In response.structured_output
In response.tool_use[0].input
questions.rationale: Plain output goes to result; schema-constrained output goes to structured_output. Parsing the wrong field is a common pipeline bug.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Migrating auth from custom JWT to either Auth0 or Cognito spans 60+ files. The two paths have different infrastructure trade-offs. Which Claude Code mode should drive the early stage?
options: Direct execution, following the senior engineer's preference
The Explore subagent on its own
Plan mode (Shift+Tab twice) before any modifications
A custom /migrate Skill the team invokes per file
questions.rationale: Multiple viable paths, architectural trade-offs, and large blast radius are the canonical plan-mode case. Plan mode separates investigation from execution, which is the discipline this change requires.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Three attempts at a webhook-to-internal-schema mapper produce inconsistent field nesting and timestamp formats. Prose instructions aren't converging. Most effective next step?
options: Re-emphasize the requirements with capitalized warnings
Set temperature to 0 to force determinism
Switch to a larger and more capable model
Provide 2-3 concrete input → output examples
questions.rationale: Concrete examples are the canonical fix when prose-based instructions produce inconsistent code. They communicate exact shape without natural-language ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your /architecture-audit Skill produces 4000 lines of correct analysis but pollutes the parent conversation's context. Frontmatter fix?
options: Make the Skill's output more concise
Run the Skill less often
context: fork to isolate execution from parent
Increase the main session's context window
questions.rationale: context: fork isolates Skill execution from the parent's context. The parent receives only the Skill's summary, not the full discovery noise.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your prompt says 'Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown.' About 9% of responses still include fences or commentary. Durable fix?
options: Use even stronger prompt language and capitals
Add 3 more few-shot examples of bare JSON
Post-process the response with a regex stripping fences
Define a tool with a JSON schema and use tool_use
questions.rationale: Prompt-level JSON instructions are probabilistic. Tool_use with a schema is structural enforcement at the API layer. Few-shot reduces but doesn't eliminate the failure; regex post-processing is brittle.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your contract extraction fabricates a value for renewal_clause when contracts have none. The field is marked required in the schema. Why?
options: The model is overconfident; lower temperature would help
The required field forces fabrication when no source value exists
Few-shot examples lack enough negative cases to teach 'missing'
The schema needs a stricter type constraint on the field
questions.rationale: Required-but-absent is the canonical fabrication trigger. The model must choose between schema violation and invention. Making the field nullable lets it return null and removes the pressure.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your retry loop tells the model 'Output was invalid, please correct.' Of 800 retries last week, ~60% failed again identically. What's missing?
options: More retry attempts (currently capped at 2)
Specific feedback: which field, expected, received
A different model on retry attempts
Lower temperature on every retry attempt
questions.rationale: Validation-retry loops only converge with actionable feedback. 'Field total: expected number, received "one hundred"' guides correction; 'invalid' is no signal.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A finance team summarizes 12,000 monthly reports nightly; results are reviewed the next morning. Lowest-cost API?
options: Real-time synchronous API for predictable latency
Prompt Caching with the real-time API
The Message Batches API
A smaller real-time model
questions.rationale: Overnight, no human waiting = textbook Batch case. Up to 24-hour window, ~50% savings, custom_id correlates inputs and outputs.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your data-cleanup workflow has Claude analyze a record, call a tool to fetch a related record, then refine. You want to move it to Batch for 50% savings. Why does it fail?
options: Batch results take longer than 24 hours typically
Tool schemas differ between Batch and real-time APIs
Batch API charges extra when tool calls are involved
Batch can't execute tools mid-request and continue
questions.rationale: Batch is async and fire-and-forget. Multi-turn tool-calling within one logical interaction requires the synchronous API.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your reviewer flags 'tests that look fragile,' producing many false positives on normal happy-path tests. Best prompt fix?
options: Lower model temperature for more conservative output
Add a confidence threshold that filters low-confidence flags
Replace 'fragile' with observable, falsifiable criteria
Increase the prompt's emphasis on being conservative
questions.rationale: Subjective adjectives invite inconsistent classification. Observable criteria ('depends on system clock, working directory, or non-deterministic ordering') give unambiguous anchors.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your review surfaces 22 findings per PR. Triage is the bottleneck; you can't drop categories. Best change without losing findings?
options: Cap findings at 8 per PR by severity
Inline reasoning and confidence on each finding
Require human review on every finding before post
Restrict reviews to security findings only
questions.rationale: Inline reasoning and confidence accelerate triage without dropping findings. Caps lose real issues; humans don't scale; restricting categories hides defects.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your code generator and reviewer are both Claude. The reviewer has the generator's full reasoning trace and frequently approves flawed code matching that rationale. Architectural fix?
options: Add extended thinking to the reviewer instance
Use a larger model for the reviewer
Have the generator self-review before submission
Reviewer runs independently without generator rationale
questions.rationale: Sharing rationale primes the reviewer to agree. Independent instances without it catch issues the generator already rationalized away. Bigger models and extended thinking don't fix bias.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 22-file PR review has inconsistent depth: detailed early, shallow late, identical patterns flagged in file 2 but approved in file 18. Best restructuring?
options: Reject PRs over 10 files entirely
Increase the model's context window
Per-file passes plus a separate integration pass
Add few-shot examples for each file type
questions.rationale: Attention dilutes across many files in one pass. Per-file passes give uniform depth; a separate integration pass catches cross-file concerns. Bigger windows don't redistribute attention.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your model returns the same content in inconsistent shapes turn-to-turn. Instructions alone aren't converging. Standard technique?
options: Stronger imperative language in the prompt
Reduce max_tokens to constrain output
Switch to a model with deterministic outputs
Provide 3-4 few-shot examples of the target shape
questions.rationale: Few-shot examples are the canonical mechanism for format calibration. They communicate exact shape without natural-language ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your CI runs `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema '...'` and reads response.result, but the validated content isn't there. Where should it look?
options: response.content[0].text
response.tool_use[0].input
response.structured_output
response.output (top-level field)
questions.rationale: Plain output goes to result; schema-constrained output goes to structured_output. A frequently tested distinction and a common pipeline bug.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Interactive assistant: 40K-token static policy preamble plus a small user query each call. Heavy traffic, users waiting. Right cost lever?
options: Trim the policy preamble as much as possible
Use a smaller model and accept some quality loss
Use the Batch API for the policy portion
Prompt Caching on the static prefix
questions.rationale: Interactive workloads can't tolerate Batch's async latency. Prompt Caching: ~90% off reads, ~25% premium on writes (5-min TTL). With heavy traffic, reads dominate and the economics work.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your support agent uses progressive summarization at 70%. In long sessions, it now misremembers order IDs and transposes dollar amounts. Right discipline?
options: Disable summarization and accept context growth
Switch to a model with a larger context window
Increase summarization aggressiveness to compress more
Pin precise facts in a stable block outside the summary
questions.rationale: Summarization is lossy for precise tokens. Pinning load-bearing facts in a stable block protects values that must remain exact, while narrative history continues to compress.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 40K-token review catches issues at the start and end but misses problems in the middle third. Name for this phenomenon?
options: Token truncation
Recency decay
Context overflow
Lost-in-the-middle
questions.rationale: Lost-in-the-middle is the named attention-distribution pattern in transformer LLMs. Larger windows don't change the shape. Mitigate structurally: edges, headers, top-of-context priming.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your extractor reports 96% aggregate accuracy. Customer complaints concentrate on credit memos. Measurement change that would have caught this?
options: Raise the aggregate accuracy bar from 96% to 99%
Add more validation rules to catch field errors
Increase the aggregate sample size substantially
Stratify accuracy by document subtype and field
questions.rationale: Aggregate metrics hide local failure. Stratified sampling reveals exactly which subtypes underperform. Raising the global bar doesn't help when bad segments are dominated by good ones.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your extractor self-rates confidence at 0.92 regardless of input quality. Leadership wants to skip human review on 'high-confidence' outputs. Prerequisite?
options: Trust the 0.92 threshold and start skipping review
Lower the routing threshold to 0.85 to be safer
Use one universal threshold across all document types
Calibrate scores against a labeled validation set
questions.rationale: Raw self-reported confidence is uncalibrated. Mapping it to actual accuracy on a labeled set turns it into a defensible routing signal. Any threshold without that is theatre.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two reputable sources cite different semiconductor capacity figures. Synthesizer flags this as contradiction; actually the sources are from different quarters. Structural fix?
options: Always pick the more recent source automatically
Use only one source per topic in the future
Require date metadata on every claim from subagents
Have an LLM judge reconcile contradictions case by case
questions.rationale: Many 'contradictions' are temporal differences. Date metadata at the claim level lets the coordinator distinguish 'X in March vs Y in October' from genuine disagreement.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your synthesis flattens everything into prose: comparisons, timelines, technical limitation lists all become paragraphs. Readers complain. Discipline?
options: Make the prose more detailed and longer
Use bullet points for every section uniformly
Render content according to its shape: tables, prose, lists
Add more section headings within the prose
questions.rationale: Content-type-appropriate rendering: tables for comparisons, prose for narrative, lists for enumerations. Flattening everything to prose hides exactly the structure readers need.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your healthcare client requires Zero Data Retention. The team wants to move overnight chart summarization to Batch for 50% savings. Why can't you?
options: Batch API doesn't support summarization tasks
Batch API isn't eligible for Zero Data Retention
Batch API would expose PHI in custom_id strings
Batch API charges extra for healthcare workloads
questions.rationale: ZDR ineligibility for Batch is a named exam fact. When ZDR is required, sync API is the only path even for non-blocking workloads. Prompt Caching remains as the cost lever.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your research subagent failed to fetch 3 of 7 sources. Synthesis writes a report using the 4 successes and presents it as complete. What discipline failed?
options: The synthesizer should have retried until they succeeded
The synthesizer should declare gaps explicitly
The synthesizer should pad with related sources to compensate
The coordinator should hide failure to maintain user trust
questions.rationale: The named rule: reports declare gaps explicitly rather than omitting them. Silent omission misrepresents the work's coverage; transparent gap declaration earns trust.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your 12-step, 2-hour compliance audit crashed at step 9 yesterday; the team re-ran the whole pipeline this morning. Which pattern provides durability?
options: Add exponential-backoff retries inside every step
Run on a machine with more memory and CPU
Persist outputs and completion to a resume manifest
Increase the timeout on every individual step
questions.rationale: Crash-recovery manifests are the named durable pattern for multi-step pipelines. Without them, every crash restarts from zero. Retries and timeouts treat symptoms, not the durability gap.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A grain-elevator inventory agent runs an agentic loop. The team wants the loop to exit cleanly once Claude has nothing more to ask for. Which response field is the canonical termination signal?
options: stop_reason is end_turn
tool_use_count equals zero
is_done is true on the last block
finish_turn appears in metadata
questions.rationale: The agentic loop pattern reads stop_reason. 'tool_use' means continue with results; 'end_turn' means the model is finished. The other field names sound plausible but are not part of the Messages API.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: On a port-logistics research system, an engineer proposes that the shipping-rates subagent call the customs-rules subagent directly to shave latency. What is the main structural objection?
options: Direct calls cost more tokens than coordinator routing
Lateral calls break the coordinator's isolation and visibility
Subagents are technically blocked from invoking other subagents
The Task tool refuses nested invocations by design
questions.rationale: Hub-and-spoke is intentional: the coordinator is the only place that sees all results, so it is the only place where deterministic conflict resolution and observability can live. Lateral calls produce hidden dependencies and untracked context.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A regulatory-filing coordinator tells its drafting subagent: 'Use the citation style we agreed on earlier.' The subagent produces inconsistent citations because the style guidance only lives in the coordinator's system prompt. What is the fix?
options: Add the citation style to a shared scratchpad file the subagent reads
Copy the citation rules verbatim into the coordinator's SubTask.context
Raise the subagent's max_tokens to give it more room to reason
Have the subagent read the coordinator's prior message history
questions.rationale: Subagents start with empty context. Anything they need has to be placed in SubTask.context by the coordinator. They do not inherit the coordinator's system prompt or message history.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A wire-transfer agent is required to call verify_kyc before move_funds. About 6% of transactions still skip verification despite a 'must always' rule in the system prompt. Which fix is structurally sound?
options: Rewrite the system prompt rule in capital letters with stronger language
Switch to a larger model that follows instructions more reliably overall
Add a tool-layer gate that rejects move_funds without prior verify_kyc
Add three more few-shot examples showing the correct ordering pattern
questions.rationale: Critical preconditions belong in deterministic enforcement, not in the prompt. Even capable models drift on a fraction of cases; a code-level guard makes the unsafe path impossible. Prompt language and few-shot reduce but cannot eliminate the failure rate.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An archaeologist asks an agent to 'investigate this newly discovered tablet collection and tell me everything interesting.' The collection's contents are unknown until exploration begins. Which decomposition pattern fits?
options: Prompt chaining with a fixed five-step pipeline applied to the whole collection
Parallel spawning of one subagent per tablet up front for maximum throughput
Dynamic adaptive decomposition where the next step depends on what prior steps uncover
A single-shot prompt asking for a complete report on the entire collection at once
questions.rationale: When the subtask graph cannot be enumerated in advance because each finding shapes the next move, dynamic decomposition is the named pattern. Fixed pipelines and parallel spawning assume known structure.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A vaccine-cold-chain audit has four tasks: (a) pull shipment manifests, (b) pull temperature logs, (c) cross-reference excursions against manifests, (d) generate the compliance report. Tasks (a) and (b) hit independent systems. What is the correct execution structure?
options: Run a, b, c, d strictly sequentially because each step depends on the previous one
Wave 1 runs a and b in parallel; Wave 2 runs c; Wave 3 runs d
Spawn all four in parallel and have the coordinator merge whatever returns
Let the model pick the order dynamically at each step of the workflow
questions.rationale: Manifests and logs are independent inputs, so they belong in the same wave. Cross-referencing needs both, so it waits. The report waits on the cross-reference. This is the canonical depends_on graph the exam tests.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A claims-triage coordinator emits one Task call per turn, waits, then emits the next. Wall-clock latency is roughly N times what it should be for N independent subagents. What change unlocks parallelism?
options: Switch fan-out to the Message Batches API for asynchronous throughput
Reduce subagents per wave so each one finishes faster sequentially
Emit N parallel Task tool calls inside a single coordinator response
Move the coordinator to a smaller, faster model for quicker turns
questions.rationale: Parallelism is a single-turn property. Multiple Task tool calls in one assistant turn run concurrently; one Task per turn forces serialization regardless of dependencies. Batch API is for offline workloads, not real-time orchestration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A discharge-summary agent at a teaching hospital omits different important pieces on different cases — sometimes follow-up labs, sometimes medication reconciliation, sometimes care-team contacts. The omissions don't follow a fixed pattern. What gives the most reliable improvement?
options: Add four representative few-shot examples of complete summaries
Add a self-critique pass against an explicit completeness checklist
Lower temperature on the drafting model so output is more consistent
Move the entire workflow to a larger model that may forget less
questions.rationale: Few-shot helps with consistent, predictable patterns. Variable per-case omissions need an explicit self-critique pass against a checklist. Temperature does not change whether the model remembers each required element.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A literature-review coordinator runs its plan once and returns whatever the subagents produced. Reviewers complain of thin coverage and missing rebuttals. Which addition is the named Domain 1.6 pattern?
options: Increase the synthesis subagent's max_tokens so it can elaborate more
Spawn more subagents per wave to broaden the initial sweep of sources
Run synthesis a second time with identical inputs for consistency
Add an EVALUATE step that scores synthesis and triggers refinement
questions.rationale: Coordinators are loops, not pipelines. The 6-step flow (PLAN, SORT, DELEGATE, EVALUATE, RESOLVE, SYNTHESIZE) includes a quality gate that triggers targeted refinement. Re-running synthesis without new inputs produces the same result.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An overnight crash interrupted a long refactor session 18 hours ago. During that window, three files the agent had open were edited by a teammate. When you resume, which approach is best?
options: Always use --resume to preserve all prior reasoning exactly as it was
Always start a fresh session with a summary because resumed sessions are unsafe
Resume the session and explicitly tell the agent which files changed on disk
Fork the session and run two parallel branches to compare outputs
questions.rationale: Resume preserves reasoning, but tool results in the history are now stale. The documented pattern is: resume, then explicitly note what changed on disk so the agent re-reads those specific files. Forking is for exploring divergent approaches, not for staleness.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A platform-migration agent has done a clean codebase analysis. The team wants to explore two competing approaches (lift-and-shift versus rewrite-in-place) from that shared baseline. Which feature fits?
options: --resume to continue the same single timeline forward
fork_session to spawn parallel branches from a shared baseline
/compact to compress context before each exploration
Open two fresh sessions and re-share the analysis output manually
questions.rationale: Forking is the named pattern for exploring divergent approaches from a shared baseline. Resume continues one timeline; compact reduces context; starting fresh duplicates effort.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coffee-roaster's coordinator spawns five subagents to answer 'what's our most-shipped SKU this week?' Each subagent does trivial work and the overhead dominates. When should a coordinator avoid decomposing?
options: Only when the user did not explicitly request subagents in the prompt
Only when the underlying model is smaller than a frontier-tier model
When coordination cost exceeds the benefit of specialization for the task
Never — coordinators should always decompose for observability and audit logs
questions.rationale: Decomposition has a cost: extra latency, extra tokens, extra coordination logic. For simple tasks a single agent call beats orchestration. The decision is about task complexity, not user phrasing or model size.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Three Wave-1 subagents run for an antitrust investigation. Two return clean results; the third hits a vendor 503. The coordinator currently aborts the entire investigation. What is the recommended discipline?
options: Abort the whole workflow on any subagent failure to avoid partial conclusions
Silently drop the failing subagent and treat its slice of results as empty
Block the wave and retry the failing subagent indefinitely until it succeeds
Proceed with available results and annotate the final report with coverage gaps
questions.rationale: Graceful degradation with explicit coverage notes is the documented pattern. Silently dropping the failure hides risk; aborting everything throws away usable work; indefinite retry burns budget. Structured error context enables the right call.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two subagents return conflicting figures for the same battery-recall scope ($88M vs $112M). The current coordinator asks Claude to 'pick the better answer.' Results vary run to run. What's the architectural fix?
options: Always pick the higher figure as a conservative default for recall scope
Apply a deterministic rule stack: reliability, recency, confidence, escalate
Have a separate LLM judge resolve every conflict on demand at runtime
Trust the figure from whichever subagent returned its result first
questions.rationale: Conflict resolution must be reproducible. A rule stack (reliability, recency, confidence, then human) yields the same answer on the same inputs. LLM-judged conflicts and 'first wins' are non-deterministic and untestable.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A market-research synthesizer receives 6,000 tokens of verbose narrative from each of four upstream subagents and runs out of context budget. The upstream subagents have unused budget. Which change addresses the imbalance?
options: Upgrade the synthesizer to a larger-context model tier and absorb the cost
Have upstream subagents return condensed structured findings, not narrative
Drop two of the four upstream subagents to reduce inbound text volume
Reduce the synthesizer's system prompt to free up tokens for inputs
questions.rationale: When downstream agents have tighter budgets, upstream agents should return condensed structured data — not their full reasoning. This is a named Domain 5.1 skill that shows up in 1.3 because subagent return shape is part of context isolation discipline.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Inside the agentic loop for a museum-archive cataloger, the model returns stop_reason of 'tool_use' with two tool_use blocks. What does the loop do next?
options: Exit the loop and return the partial response immediately to the user
Ignore the tool calls and re-prompt the model with stricter system instructions
Call the model again right away without running the requested tools
Execute the tools, append the tool_result blocks, and call the model again
questions.rationale: tool_use is the 'I need information' signal. The runtime executes the requested tool calls, appends their results, and re-invokes the model. The loop terminates only on end_turn (or an error stop_reason).
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A real-estate-listings agent has two tools: search_mls (live listings) and lookup_historical_sale (past closings). The model occasionally calls search_mls when users ask about a sale from 2019. Descriptions are otherwise solid. What addition reliably stops the misroute?
options: Increase the system prompt's emphasis on accuracy and care in routing decisions
Add negative bounds to search_mls excluding historical sales and pointing elsewhere
Lower temperature on the agent so its tool selections become more deterministic
Have the agent always call both tools on every turn and merge their results
questions.rationale: Negative bounds with a pointer to the right alternative is the documented description pattern for adjacent tools. Calling both is wasteful; temperature does not change tool routing; vague prompt emphasis does not generalize.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A generic process_record tool handles claim creation, claim status lookup, claim cancellation, and document attachment. Routing reliability has degraded as more capabilities accumulated. What is the right structural move?
options: Write a longer description that enumerates and explains all four subcases clearly
Add four to six few-shot examples covering each subcase routing pattern
Split into purpose-specific tools, each with its own input/output contract
Force the generic tool with tool_choice on every turn of the conversation
questions.rationale: Generic tools that do too many things fail predictably as variants accumulate. The structural fix is splitting along purpose with crisp input/output contracts per tool. Description length and few-shot are bandages.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A patent-search tool returns the same string 'no_data' both when the search service times out and when the search ran successfully but matched zero patents. The agent retries on both. What is missing?
options: More aggressive retry with longer exponential backoff between attempts
Distinct response shapes for successful-empty versus access-failure outcomes
A larger maximum result-set limit configured on the underlying search service
A different model whose interpretation of the literal string 'no_data' is sharper
questions.rationale: Empty results and access failures look identical in the naive case but require opposite responses. The fix is structured error metadata: 'success with zero results' versus 'access failure, isRetryable: true'. Retrying a valid empty result wastes budget.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A hospitality booking tool refuses to refund a stay outside the 30-day window. Policy says the refund cannot be granted. Which errorCategory should the structured error carry?
options: transient
validation
permission
business
questions.rationale: Refund-window violations are policy rules, not technical failures. Business errors are non-retryable and should carry a customer-friendly explanation. Transient is retryable; validation is bad input; permission is auth or scope problems.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An engineering-support agent has accumulated 22 tools spanning incident triage, deploy pipelines, and observability. Tool-selection accuracy has dropped noticeably. What's the recommended structural change?
options: Rewrite all 22 tool descriptions in a single coordinated pass for clarity
Add detailed few-shot examples of correct tool selections across the toolset
Decompose into specialized subagents with 4–5 scoped tools per subagent
Force a specific tool with tool_choice on every turn to constrain selection
questions.rationale: Attention fragmentation is real and measurable past roughly 8 tools. Descriptions cannot overcome it. The documented fix is decomposition into specialized subagents, each carrying 4-5 focused tools.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An e-discovery pipeline must always call classify_document_type before any extraction tool. Sometimes the model skips classification and goes straight to extraction. What enforces the order on the first turn?
options: tool_choice: 'auto' combined with a stronger system prompt instruction
tool_choice: 'any' so the model is forced to call some tool first
tool_choice set to the named classify_document_type tool on the first turn
Set tool_choice to 'required' and list classify_document_type first in the schema
questions.rationale: Only the named-tool form guarantees a specific tool runs first. 'any' forces some tool but the model picks; 'auto' is fully discretionary; ordering in the tool list does not bind selection.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A fact-checking system wants to expose a curated registry of source domains with reliability ratings. Agents read the registry to inform routing but never modify it. What MCP primitive fits?
options: Tool, because agents query it on every turn
Resource, because it is read-only context with no execution
Prompt template, because it parameterizes how facts are checked
A hybrid combining tool execution with resource semantics
questions.rationale: Read-only catalogs (source registries, schemas, document indexes) are Resources. They reduce exploratory tool calls by letting agents see what exists. Tools execute; Resources are read.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two engineers on a power-grid analytics team each configure the same shared OPC-UA MCP server in their personal ~/.claude.json files. A new teammate has none of it configured. Where should the shared server live?
options: Keep it in personal ~/.claude.json and document the steps in a team wiki
Project-level .mcp.json with environment-variable expansion for credentials
Email the JSON snippet to every new joiner during their onboarding week
Use a single shared user account on a jump host that everyone logs into
questions.rationale: Project-shared MCP servers belong in .mcp.json under version control. Use ${ENV_VAR} expansion for secrets so credentials are not committed. ~/.claude.json is for personal or experimental servers.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude Code's Edit operation is failing on a configuration file because the target string appears in 11 locations. What's the canonical fallback?
options: Use Bash with sed -i to do a global in-place substitution across the file
Read the file, modify the content in context, then Write it back
Call Edit repeatedly on the same target string until one of the calls succeeds
Switch to a regex-based search tool that handles non-unique matches natively
questions.rationale: Edit requires a unique match. When that fails, Read + Write is the documented universal fallback: load the file, modify in context, write back. Loose sed substitution risks unintended edits; retrying Edit without uniqueness does not help.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Tool descriptions are confirmed unambiguous, but whenever a user mentions 'subscription' the model still routes to get_customer_profile instead of lookup_subscription_plan. Where is the root cause most likely?
options: The descriptions still have residual semantic overlap and need further tightening
Keyword-sensitive routing instructions in the system prompt override the descriptions
The model has a training bias that favors customer tools on subscription vocabulary
The two tools should be merged into one combined endpoint with shared semantics
questions.rationale: When descriptions are stipulated as good, look upstream. System prompts often contain instructions like 'when users mention subscription, gather customer info first' that override descriptions on specific keywords. Rewriting good descriptions ignores the actual cause.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A weather-data subagent in a wildfire-risk system propagates every transient 503 from its upstream API straight to the coordinator. The coordinator now spends most of its time orchestrating retries the subagent could handle locally. What's the proper discipline?
options: Always escalate every error to the coordinator for centralized visibility
Retry transient failures locally and escalate only what cannot be resolved
Silently suppress transient errors and return the most recent cached value
Move all retry logic to the coordinator and remove subagent error handling
questions.rationale: Errors are best handled at the lowest level capable of resolving them. Transient errors retry locally; only unresolvable failures escalate, and they carry attempt history so the coordinator has context.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A defense contractor's compliance office needs every developer to enforce a 'no third-party HTTP calls in classified directories' rule. Developers must not be able to override it. Which CLAUDE.md scope fits?
options: Project-level at ./CLAUDE.md committed to version control
User-level at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for each developer
Managed/Org level deployed by IT to the OS system directory
Local override at ./CLAUDE.local.md kept out of version control
questions.rationale: Managed/Org-level CLAUDE.md (the OS system directory level) has the highest precedence and cannot be overridden by lower levels. Project-level can be edited by developers; user and local levels are personal.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A new joiner at an ag-tech startup reports that Claude Code is suggesting patterns that contradict the team's documented standards. The standards live in ./CLAUDE.md. What's the first diagnostic command to run on the joiner's machine?
options: /init to regenerate the project CLAUDE.md from scratch on the laptop
/compact to reset the current session's working context immediately
/memory to inspect which memory files are loaded and at which scope
/clear to wipe local state and start a brand new conversation
questions.rationale: /memory reports the active memory files and their hierarchy. It's the canonical diagnostic for 'why is Claude Code behaving inconsistently with my expectations.' /init creates a new file; /compact reduces context; /clear is unrelated.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A /codebase-map skill on a 1.2M-line monorepo produces 6,000 lines of analysis that is useful to read but should not pollute the main session's context for later edits. Which SKILL.md frontmatter option fixes this?
options: allowed-tools restricted to Read only for the duration of the skill
context: fork to run the skill in an isolated subagent context
argument-hint to label the skill output as large before invocation
disable-model-invocation: true to block the model from auto-triggering
questions.rationale: context: fork is the named option for isolating verbose or exploratory skill output. The subagent does the work; only a summary returns to the main session. allowed-tools restricts tool access; argument-hint is a UX label; disable-model-invocation blocks auto-triggering.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your codebase has a 'generate database migration' workflow that should run only when a developer explicitly invokes it — not as ambient guidance on every prompt. Where does this belong?
options: Appended to ./CLAUDE.md as a section developers can reference when needed
A Skill at .claude/skills/generate-migration/SKILL.md invoked on demand
A path-scoped rule at .claude/rules/migrations.md tied to migration glob paths
A section inside the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for personal preference
questions.rationale: CLAUDE.md is always-loaded standards. Skills are on-demand workflows. A migration generator is a task-specific workflow, which is the textbook Skill use case. Path-scoped rules are for editing-time conventions, not workflows.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your conventions for Cypress end-to-end specs apply to files matching **/*.cy.ts, but those files are scattered across the repo under different feature folders. What's the cleanest mechanism?
options: Drop a CLAUDE.md in every folder that contains *.cy.ts files in the tree
A single .claude/rules/cypress.md with frontmatter paths matching *.cy.ts
Add the rules to the root CLAUDE.md so they always load with the project
Require developers to invoke a slash command before editing any test file
questions.rationale: Path-specific rules with glob patterns load only on matching files, regardless of directory. That's exactly the case for conventions that follow a file type spread across the codebase. Per-folder CLAUDE.md files duplicate maintenance; root CLAUDE.md wastes tokens on irrelevant edits.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A backend developer asks Claude Code to 'add a null check to the line that parses request.body.email in handlers/signup.ts.' Which mode fits?
options: Plan mode, because every modification should be planned before execution
Direct execution for a single-file, well-scoped change with no tradeoffs
Plan mode followed by the Explore subagent for full architectural review
Forking the session to try the change in two competing parallel branches
questions.rationale: Plan mode is for complex changes with multiple valid approaches, large-scale refactors, or architectural decisions. A single-file null check is the canonical direct-execution case. Forking and Explore are overkill.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Mid-refactor, your main Claude Code session is bloated with grep dumps from broad codebase exploration. You still need to keep exploring while preserving the main session's working context. Which feature fits?
options: /compact to compress the current session's context window in place
The Explore subagent, which runs read-only discovery in a separate context
fork_session to spawn a parallel branch dedicated to the next discovery query
Open a new top-level Claude Code instance and re-share the relevant state
questions.rationale: Explore is the named pattern for read-only discovery offloaded into an isolated context. /compact compresses but still pollutes; forking duplicates the working state. Explore is purpose-built for this.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Three attempts at a payroll-tax calculator produce different field names and rounding rules each time, despite a paragraph of prose description. Which refinement technique converges fastest?
options: Repeat the prose description more emphatically with stronger imperative verbs
Provide concrete input/output examples that fix names and rounding
Switch to a different model on each attempt and compare the three outputs
Lower temperature to zero on every iteration and accept reduced variation
questions.rationale: When prose alone gives the model latitude to drift, examples bind the contract. Two or three concrete I/O pairs eliminate ambiguity that paragraphs cannot. Temperature and model swaps do not address spec ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An e-bike-rental startup added Claude Code to its GitHub Actions PR review workflow with the command `claude "review changes"`. The job times out at 60 minutes with no output. Same prompt runs fine locally. What is missing?
options: An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable that the runner has not exported
The -p (or --print) flag for non-interactive mode in CI environments
A larger Actions runner with more CPU and memory to handle the workload
A retry strategy in the workflow YAML to recover from transient failures
questions.rationale: Without -p, Claude Code starts its interactive terminal UI and waits for user input. CI has no user, so the process hangs until job timeout. -p is the canonical non-interactive flag.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A nightly compliance scanner runs Claude Code in CI. Security wants Claude limited to Read and Grep — no Bash, no Edit, no anything else. Which flag accomplishes the actual restriction?
options: --allowedTools 'Read,Grep', which pre-approves only the two listed tools
--tools 'Read,Grep', which restricts the available toolset to those two only
--bare alone, which strips unsafe defaults from the runtime environment
An entry in CLAUDE.md instructing Claude not to use any tool besides Read
questions.rationale: --tools is the restriction flag — anything not listed is unavailable. --allowedTools only suppresses permission prompts; the tools remain reachable. Prompt-level instructions don't constrain capability. --bare disables auto-discovery but doesn't restrict tools.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A code-review CI job behaves differently on each developer's local machine than on the CI runner because everyone's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, hooks, and MCP servers leak into the run. Which flag normalizes the environment?
options: --isolated, which sandboxes the process from other host configuration
--bare, which skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, MCP, memory, and CLAUDE.md
--clean, which clears cached state from prior runs of the same job
--no-config, which disables every config file the runtime would otherwise read
questions.rationale: --bare is Anthropic's recommended CI flag for reproducibility. It strips all the auto-discovery that makes local convenient but CI unpredictable. Documentation notes --bare will become the default for -p in a future release.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your team wants a /release-notes command that everyone gets automatically when they clone the repo. Where does the command file belong?
options: ~/.claude/commands/release-notes.md so each developer has it locally
.claude/commands/release-notes.md committed to project version control
Inline inside the root CLAUDE.md as a procedural instruction to follow
A Skill with disable-model-invocation: true to prevent any auto-trigger
questions.rationale: .claude/commands/ is the project-shared, version-controlled scope. ~/.claude/commands/ is personal and not shared. Commands belong in commands/, not in CLAUDE.md or skills/.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)
