questions.text: A safety reviewer for industrial-equipment manuals uses the instruction 'flag anything that seems risky.' False positives are flooding the queue. What's the right rewrite?
options: Add a softening clause like 'be conservative — flag only clearly risky items'
Replace it with explicit categorical criteria listing which hazard types to flag
Lower the model temperature so flagging decisions become more consistent
Use a smaller model that tends to flag less aggressively by default
questions.rationale: Vague instructions like 'risky' or 'be conservative' make the model guess what counts. Explicit categorical criteria with examples is the documented improvement. Temperature and model size do not fix definitional ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An extraction agent processes purchase orders from 14 vendors. Some put quantities in a column, some inline, some in a comments field. Detailed prose instructions produce ~76% accuracy. What's the right next move?
options: Add a fourth paragraph of prose enumerating every layout variant the vendors use
Provide three to four few-shot examples that span the major format variants
Restrict input to a single canonical template and reject the others upstream
Drop temperature to zero so the extractor's behavior becomes deterministic
questions.rationale: Few-shot examples teach generalization for ambiguous-case handling and varied document structures. Two to four examples covering the variant range is the documented sweet spot. More prose does not generalize the way examples do.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer adds three few-shot examples showing the model always calling check_inventory before reserve_item, hoping examples enforce that ordering. Is this a sound use of few-shot?
options: Yes — few-shot is the standard mechanism for binding execution order on tools
No — few-shot demonstrates format and judgment but does not enforce tool order
Yes, as long as the developer provides at least five examples for reliability
No initially, but more examples eventually make tool ordering reliable enough
questions.rationale: Few-shot is a guidance layer, not an enforcement layer. Tool execution order is enforced by tool_choice or programmatic gates, not by examples. Adding more examples does not make probabilistic guidance deterministic.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A municipal-permit extractor needs every response to be schema-valid JSON. The current prompt says 'always return JSON matching the schema' and roughly 7% of outputs contain prose preambles. What's the structural fix?
options: Stronger prompt language with capitalized warnings against any extra preamble text
Define a tool whose schema is the input, and force the call with tool_choice
Post-process responses with a regex that strips prose preambles before parsing
Add five more few-shot examples showing bare JSON output with no prose around it
questions.rationale: Prompt-only JSON instructions are probabilistic. tool_use with a strict schema is structural enforcement at the API layer and eliminates JSON syntax errors by construction. Regex post-processing is brittle; few-shot reduces but doesn't eliminate the failure.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A bill-of-lading extractor's schema marks customs_broker as a required string field. About 11% of shipments have no broker, and the model fabricates plausible-looking names for those cases. Why?
options: Temperature is too high — lower it and the fabrication rate will drop materially
Required-but-absent forces a choice between schema violation and invention
Few-shot examples are missing negative cases where the broker is null in the document
The schema needs a tighter maxLength constraint on the customs_broker field type
questions.rationale: Required-but-absent is the canonical fabrication trigger. The model must satisfy the schema, so when the source has nothing, it invents. Making the field nullable lets it return null cleanly. This is a named Domain 4.3 trap.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An invoice-extraction retry loop sends 'Output was invalid, please correct.' Of 1,200 retries last month, 58% failed identically a second time. What change makes retries converge?
options: Raise the maximum retry cap from 2 to 6 attempts per failed extraction record
Use a different, larger model on retry while keeping the same generic message
Make the retry message specific: name the field, type, and what was received
Lower temperature on retry attempts to encourage more conservative output choices
questions.rationale: Validation-retry loops only converge with actionable feedback. 'Field invoice_total: expected number, received "one hundred fifty"' guides correction. Generic 'invalid' is no signal at all. Raising the retry cap multiplies the same wasted call.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An extractor keeps failing to find a contract_renewal_date because the source contract does not contain one. The retry loop has tried 4 times with detailed feedback. What's the right behavior?
options: Increase the retry cap to 10 attempts and let the loop continue searching
Lower the temperature to zero and retry once more before declaring failure
Stop retrying and either return null or route to a human for resolution
Switch to a larger, more capable model and run another four retry attempts
questions.rationale: Retry recovers from format and structural errors. It cannot recover information that is not in the source. The documented pattern is: return null for nullable fields, or escalate to a human if the field is required.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A media-monitoring team submits 8,000 articles to the Message Batches API overnight. When results come back, how do they correlate each output with its input?
options: By relying on response array order, which mirrors the original input array order
By the custom_id provided with each request, which is echoed back on every response
By computing and comparing message hashes of input prompts against response text
By submitting one batch per article and naming each batch with the article identifier
questions.rationale: custom_id is the correlation key for the Message Batches API. The response order is not guaranteed; relying on positional matching is unsafe. Hashing is unnecessary when the API provides the correlator.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A research workflow needs Claude to read an abstract, call fetch_full_paper, then summarize using both. The team wants to move to the Batch API for the 50% discount. Why is this incompatible?
options: Batch results sometimes take longer than the 24-hour processing window allows
Batch is asynchronous; it cannot run a tool mid-request and continue reasoning
Batch charges extra per tool call, which erodes most of the discount in practice
Tool schemas accepted by Batch differ subtly from the real-time API schemas
questions.rationale: Batch is fundamentally async. Any workflow needing multi-turn tool calling within one logical interaction must use the synchronous API. This is a named, frequently tested exam fact.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An interactive legal-research assistant sends a 35K-token statute corpus as a system preamble plus a small per-call user query. Traffic is heavy and users are waiting. Which cost lever fits?
options: Use the Batch API for the static prefix and accept the asynchronous latency
Trim the statute corpus aggressively and rely on retrieval for missing context
Apply Prompt Caching on the static statute prefix to discount the repeated reads
Switch the assistant to a smaller model tier and accept the reduction in quality
questions.rationale: Interactive workloads can't tolerate Batch's async latency. Prompt Caching is the right lever for repeated static prefixes on a real-time path. Cache reads are ~90% cheaper; writes carry a ~25% premium. With heavy traffic, reads dominate and savings are large.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A code-generation pipeline uses the same Claude session to generate and then review its own output. Reviewers note that subtle bugs slip through despite the review step. What's the structural fix?
options: Increase max_tokens on the review pass so it has more room to be thorough
Have a fresh, independent Claude instance with no prior context do the review
Have the same session review its output twice in a row to catch missed defects
Add a third self-review pass by the same session for diminishing-returns coverage
questions.rationale: Self-review by the same instance retains the reasoning context that produced the code, which biases the reviewer toward seeing the design as correct. An independent instance with no prior context applies fresh scrutiny. This is the named Domain 4.6 pattern.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Code reviews of 28-file PRs show inconsistent depth — detailed feedback on early files, surface notes on later files, missed cross-file issues entirely. Why, and what's the fix?
options: The PR exceeds context capacity; increase the context window to the next tier
Attention dilutes across many files; do per-file passes then an integration pass
The reviewer is too random; lower temperature to make critique more consistent
The current model is too weak; move review onto the next tier of model entirely
questions.rationale: Attention quality degrades when many files share one context. Per-file passes keep each context narrow; an integration pass then handles cross-file checks with a clean job. Larger windows do not change attention distribution.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An order-history tool returns 42 fields per record. The agent only uses 4 of them, but the full payload accumulates in context across turns and crowds out everything else. What's the discipline?
options: Move to a model whose context window is large enough to absorb the payload
Trim tool outputs at the tool layer to only the fields the agent actually uses
Instruct the agent to ignore irrelevant fields in its downstream reasoning steps
Raise summarization aggressiveness so the verbose payloads compress sooner
questions.rationale: Trimming tool outputs to relevant fields at the tool layer is the named Domain 5.1 skill. Telling the model to ignore fields it has already seen does not free the tokens; larger windows just delay the problem.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A long-running tax-prep session uses progressive summarization. After several hours, the agent starts misremembering filing IDs and transposing dollar amounts. What's the right discipline?
options: Disable summarization entirely and accept whatever context growth that produces
Pin precise facts (IDs, dates, amounts) in a stable case-facts block on every prompt
Switch to a model with a larger context window so summarization rarely triggers
Increase summarization aggressiveness so the model relies on it less often overall
questions.rationale: Summarization is fine for narrative context and brutal for precise tokens. Pinning load-bearing facts in a stable block outside the summary protects values that must remain exact while narrative history continues to compress.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A customer writes: 'Stop. I don't want any more questions. Please transfer me to a human supervisor now.' The agent still has two diagnostic tools it could run. What's the right behavior?
options: Run the diagnostics first so the human supervisor receives more context up front
Honor the explicit request immediately and hand off with a concise summary
Ask the customer to try one more troubleshooting step before any transfer occurs
Continue autonomously as long as the underlying issue looks easy to resolve
questions.rationale: An explicit customer request for a human is a hard escalation trigger. Do not delay with more investigation. This is consistently tested and the trap answer is always 'investigate first.'
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A customer writes: 'This is absolutely the worst experience ever, fix my order right now or else.' The order is in a state the agent can resolve via standard policy. What's the right behavior?
options: Escalate to a human supervisor immediately because the sentiment is very negative
Acknowledge the frustration and offer to resolve within policy on this turn
Run all the diagnostic tools first, then escalate because the customer sounds angry
Cite the relevant policy section and politely decline to engage with the customer
questions.rationale: Frustration and an explicit demand for a human are different signals. Sentiment alone is not a complexity signal; the right move is acknowledge plus offer to resolve, and escalate only if the customer reiterates the preference.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A lookup for 'Maria Garcia' returns three matching customer records. What should the agent do?
options: Pick the record with the most recent account activity in the last 90 days
Pick by name similarity against phonetic and accent-tolerant variants
Ask the customer for an additional identifier and let them disambiguate themselves
Pick the record with the most lifetime orders since it is most likely the real one
questions.rationale: Heuristic selection on customer matches is a privacy and accuracy risk. Asking for a second identifier and letting the user disambiguate is the documented pattern. All the heuristic options are listed traps.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A research subagent returns 'search unavailable' on any failure. The coordinator can't decide whether to retry, fall back to another source, or annotate a coverage gap. What payload does it need?
options: A longer free-text message that describes the failure in more readable detail
A structured envelope with failure type, attempt, partial results, and alternatives
A full exception traceback with stack frames passed back to the coordinator agent
Nothing extra — the coordinator should retry every error indefinitely until success
questions.rationale: Generic failure strings hide the information needed for recovery. The documented structured-error envelope (type, attempt, partial results, alternatives) is what lets the coordinator retry intelligently, fall back, or annotate gaps. Tracebacks are noise to the model.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A loan-application extractor self-rates its confidence at 0.93 on virtually every record. The team wants to use that score to skip human review on high-confidence cases. What discipline applies first?
options: Trust the score and reduce reviewer staffing at the 0.90 threshold next quarter
Calibrate self-reported confidence against a labeled validation set first
Lower the routing threshold to 0.85 as a safety margin and roll out gradually
Use a single universal threshold for every field type across the whole pipeline
questions.rationale: Raw self-reported confidence is uncalibrated. The named Domain 5.5 discipline is calibration against a labeled set: '0.85 model confidence corresponds to 92% accuracy on this document type.' Without that, any threshold is theater.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A medical-claims extractor reports 97% accuracy overall. Provider complaints concentrate on one specific category: dental codes. What measurement discipline would have caught this earlier?
options: Increase the validation sample size and recompute the same aggregate accuracy
Report stratified accuracy by document type and field so segments don't hide
Switch to a different model whose overall accuracy number is somewhat higher
Lower the confidence threshold that routes records to human review next quarter
questions.rationale: Aggregate numbers hide segment failures. Stratified sampling and per-segment accuracy reporting surface the categories where the system actually breaks. This is a named Domain 5.5 skill that the exam tests directly.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A research subagent failed to fetch 4 of 11 sources. The synthesis writes a confident-sounding report and never mentions the missing sources. What's the discipline?
options: Suppress mentions of failures so the final report reads clean and decisive
Pass coverage metadata to synthesis and require the report to enumerate gaps
Re-run only the failed sources until every one of them eventually succeeds
Reduce reliance on multiple sources and switch to a single trusted provider
questions.rationale: A report that silently omits failed sources hides risk. The documented pattern is explicit coverage gap reporting in the final output. Indefinite retry burns budget without guaranteeing success; collapsing to a single source destroys triangulation.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A support agent can resolve simple replacement requests, but when a customer asks about a missing package, a billing adjustment, and account access in one message, the agent repeatedly calls customer lookup for each issue and takes 14 tool calls. What change best addresses the root cause?

Decompose the message into distinct concerns, gather shared customer context once, investigate concerns in parallel, then synthesize one response.
Add stronger prompt language telling the agent to avoid redundant tool calls.
Create a single generic investigate_request tool that hides all backend systems from Claude.
questions.rationale: The problem is structural: multi-concern requests are being handled sequentially with redundant context gathering. Decomposition with shared context and parallel investigation reduces tool calls while preserving coverage.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your agent confuses get_customer and lookup_order because both tools say only 'retrieves information' and both accept string identifiers. What is the highest-leverage first fix?

Force lookup_order whenever the user provides any number.
Rewrite tool descriptions with expected inputs, example queries, edge cases, outputs, and explicit boundaries between the two tools.
Merge the tools into lookup_anything so Claude has fewer choices.
questions.rationale: Tool descriptions are the primary routing signal. Clear names, input expectations, examples, and boundaries fix the root cause without bypassing model reasoning.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

Process both records and explain that the customer can correct any mistake.
Escalate every duplicate-name case immediately without asking follow-up questions.

questions.text: The PR bot sometimes returns markdown, sometimes prose, and sometimes JSON. Downstream posting code needs a consistent schema. What is the strongest approach?
options: Ask politely for JSON in the prompt.
Use structured JSON output with a schema for review findings.
Parse all possible formats with regular expressions.
Tell developers to manually clean the output.
questions.rationale: CI needs machine-readable, schema-constrained output rather than best-effort formatting instructions.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A review bot flags intentional type assertions and correct error handling as issues despite a general instruction to 'be conservative.' What is the best improvement?
options: Provide targeted few-shot examples of those false-positive patterns and the correct non-flagging behavior.
Increase max_tokens so Claude can think longer.
Report only findings with self-rated confidence above 50%.
Disable review of TypeScript files.
questions.rationale: Few-shot examples are effective for calibrating ambiguous review judgments and reducing specific false positive patterns.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 16-file pull request receives shallow and inconsistent review comments. Some cross-file API mismatches are missed. What review architecture is best?
options: One giant review prompt with all files and stricter instructions.
Per-file local review passes followed by a separate cross-file integration pass.
Review only the largest changed file.
Ask the author to summarize the PR first.
questions.rationale: Multi-pass review reduces attention dilution: local passes catch file-level issues, and integration passes catch cross-file problems.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: The same issue is posted again every time a PR is updated. How should reruns avoid duplicate comments?
options: Include prior automated findings in context and instruct Claude to report only new or still-unresolved issues.
Use a new session ID for every CI run.
Deduplicate comments only by exact string match after generation.
Never review files that were previously commented on.
questions.rationale: Prior findings in context let Claude behave like an incremental reviewer and avoid duplicate feedback at generation time.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: The same Claude session writes a patch and then reviews it. The review is lenient and misses obvious weaknesses. What change improves objectivity?
options: Use an independent reviewer instance that does not inherit the generation context.
Ask the same session to be more critical.
Increase temperature for the review.
Use a longer final answer format.
questions.rationale: Independent review instances reduce self-review bias caused by retaining generation reasoning context.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A manager proposes using Message Batches for blocking pre-merge review checks because it is cheaper. What should you recommend?
options: Use batches for blocking CI checks because cost is most important.
Use real-time Claude Code/API calls for blocking CI; reserve batches for latency-tolerant overnight evaluation.
Use batches only for markdown output.
Disable CI reviews entirely.
questions.rationale: Blocking CI needs timely feedback. Message Batches are appropriate for non-blocking, latency-tolerant workloads.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A PR-review prompt asks Claude to list every possible improvement. Developers complain about style nitpicks and low signal. What prompt objective is better for CI?
options: Report only actionable bugs, security issues, broken tests, API contract problems, or risky regressions; avoid style preferences unless requested.
Report at least ten findings per PR.
Prioritize formatting issues because they are easy to fix.
Avoid severity labels so feedback feels less harsh.
questions.rationale: CI review should be conservative and actionable, prioritizing real defects over speculative or stylistic comments.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: CI results vary by developer machine because local Claude Code memories, hooks, and MCP servers affect behavior. What helps produce deterministic containerized CI behavior?
options: Use bare/configuration-free execution where appropriate and supply required CI configuration explicitly.
Rely on each developer's local ~/.claude settings.
Ask developers to synchronize their personal memories weekly.
Use more verbose prompts.
questions.rationale: CI should not depend on personal local configuration. Bare/configuration-controlled execution improves reproducibility.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: You want to evaluate 80 mocked timeout and permission-denial scenarios overnight to test error handling. What mechanism is appropriate?
options: Message Batches with programmatic requests for non-blocking evaluation.
A blocking PR check for every scenario.
Manual testing through the chat UI.
A single prompt asking Claude to imagine all failures.
questions.rationale: Batch processing is well suited for large, latency-tolerant evaluation suites and edge-case testing.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Invoices often omit purchase order numbers. The model fabricates plausible PO numbers because the schema requires a string. What schema change is best?
options: Make the PO number nullable so Claude can return null when absent.
Require 'N/A' as the string for missing values.
Remove validation entirely.
Ask Claude to guess only when confident.
questions.rationale: Nullable fields give the model a valid way to represent absence, reducing fabrication.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A document classification enum has invoice, contract, receipt, and memo. Unknown documents are forced into the nearest category. What pattern handles this better?
options: Remove the enum and use free text only.
Add an 'other' enum value paired with a detail field describing the specific type.
Add twenty speculative categories.
Route every unknown-looking document to failure.
questions.rationale: The 'other' + detail string pattern preserves structure while giving an escape hatch for unanticipated categories.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An extraction must always return exactly one JSON object as the assistant response, not a tool call. Which mechanism best fits?
options: Response-level structured output with json_schema/strict configuration.
A vague prompt saying 'return JSON only'.
A tool definition for an unrelated action.
Markdown with code fences.
questions.rationale: When the entire response must conform to a schema, response-level structured output is the direct fit.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An extraction tool accepts a nested line_items array. Claude often malforms item objects. What tool-definition improvement helps most?
options: Add input examples showing correctly structured nested objects.
Flatten everything into one text field.
Remove line items from the schema.
Retry silently without feedback.
questions.rationale: Concrete input examples help the model construct complex nested tool inputs correctly.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Your system reports 97% overall accuracy, but invoices from one vendor fail tax_amount 25% of the time. What evaluation gap does this reveal?
options: The overall sample size is too small only.
Aggregate accuracy is masking segment-level failures; evaluate by document type/vendor and field.
The model should never extract tax fields.
The passing threshold should be lowered.
questions.rationale: Stratified evaluation by document type, vendor, and field reveals hidden failure modes masked by aggregate metrics.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: The model outputs confidence scores for extracted fields. How should those scores be used safely?
options: Trust them directly as probabilities.
Calibrate them against labeled validation sets and set thresholds per document type and field.
Ignore them completely in all workflows.
Use a single universal threshold for every field.
questions.rationale: Raw self-reported confidence needs calibration. Thresholds should reflect segment-specific risk and historical accuracy.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A validation retry loop keeps failing because line items sum to $91.40 but the document states a total of $94.10. Line items were extracted correctly. What should the system infer?
options: Retry indefinitely until the total matches.
The source document may contain a discrepancy; route or flag for human review instead of forcing a correction.
Delete one line item.
Lower the schema precision.
questions.rationale: Retries cannot fix contradictions in the source. Preserve the discrepancy and route according to policy.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A contract extraction schema has a required termination_clause field. Draft contracts sometimes have no such clause, and Claude invents one. What is best?
options: Make termination_clause nullable and require evidence when present.
Tell Claude that fabrication is bad.
Post-process invented clauses with regex.
Always classify drafts as invalid.
questions.rationale: Nullable fields plus evidence requirements reduce fabrication and make absence explicit.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: High-confidence extractions are auto-approved, but you still want to detect new systematic errors after a prompt change. What should you add?
options: Stratified random sampling of high-confidence outputs for audit.
Review only low-confidence outputs.
Stop collecting reviewer outcomes.
Use only aggregate weekly accuracy.
questions.rationale: Sampling apparently safe outputs is necessary to detect drift and hidden high-confidence errors.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A downstream system rejects extracted records because missing optional fields are omitted inconsistently. What output design is best?
options: Use a clear schema contract specifying nullable/optional behavior and validate before sending downstream.
Let each prompt decide field presence.
Send prose summaries instead of JSON.
Have downstream systems infer missing values.
questions.rationale: Reliable integration requires an explicit schema contract and validation so missing data is represented consistently.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A logistics agent receives a Claude response with two tool_use blocks: check_inventory and estimate_freight. The harness currently executes only the first block and asks Claude what to do next. What should the loop do instead?
options: Execute all requested tools, return their tool_result blocks together, then continue the loop
Execute the first tool, summarize the result, and ask Claude whether the second tool is still needed
Treat multiple tool_use blocks as a planning error and ask Claude to choose a single tool
Convert the tool_use blocks into assistant text so the model can reason about them later
questions.rationale: Multiple independent tool calls in the same response should be executed by the application and returned together in the next user message. Running only the first tool creates unnecessary turns and can break the model’s intended parallel plan. The other options either turn structured tool calls into prose or add extra model decisions that are not needed.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A research coordinator produces a strong report on hospital staffing costs but omits patient-safety regulations, even though every spawned subagent completed its assignment. Logs show the coordinator assigned labor, payroll, and scheduling subtasks only. What failed?
options: The synthesis agent should have searched for missing sections after drafting the report
The coordinator under-scoped the work during task decomposition
The labor subagent needed broader web-search permissions for policy sources
The report generator should have used a larger context window for all outputs
questions.rationale: The subagents did what they were asked to do, so the failure sits with the coordinator’s decomposition. It scoped a broad healthcare operations topic into only staffing-cost subtasks. More tools or context for downstream agents would not recover domains that were never assigned.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator passes a synthesis subagent only a one-paragraph summary of three prior market-analysis agents. The final answer loses source URLs, publication dates, and which claim came from which report. What should the coordinator pass instead?
options: The raw transcripts from every prior agent, with no filtering or restructuring
A short executive summary and instructions to preserve attribution where possible
Structured findings that separate claims, source metadata, dates, and confidence
A pointer to the coordinator conversation so the synthesis agent can inspect history
questions.rationale: Subagents do not inherit the coordinator’s full context, so the coordinator must package what matters explicitly. Structured claim-source payloads preserve provenance and temporal metadata while avoiding raw transcript bloat. A pointer to hidden coordinator history is not a valid context-passing mechanism.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A travel-refund agent may verify booking ownership, check fare rules, and inspect disruption notices in any order. It must never issue a voucher until all three checks are complete. Which architecture best fits this?
options: A fixed prompt chain that always verifies ownership, then fare rules, then disruption notices, then vouchers
A classifier that routes refund requests into one of four hardcoded voucher workflows
A prompt instruction that the voucher tool should be called only after all checks are done
Model-driven investigation with a programmatic gate before the issue_voucher tool
questions.rationale: The preliminary checks can happen in flexible order, so a rigid pipeline adds needless constraint. The sensitive action needs deterministic enforcement, which a gate or hook provides. A prompt instruction alone still has a non-zero failure rate for critical workflow ordering.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A claims agent reads dates from three MCP tools: one returns Unix seconds, one returns ISO 8601 strings, and one returns MM/DD/YYYY text. The model keeps comparing dates incorrectly. Where should the fix live?
options: A PostToolUse hook that normalizes date fields before Claude sees the results
A stronger system prompt listing every date format used by each backend
A user-facing warning that dates may be approximate across systems without adding a deterministic validation boundary
A separate date-review subagent that checks every answer after generation
questions.rationale: This is a deterministic data-normalization problem, not a reasoning preference. A PostToolUse hook can transform heterogeneous tool outputs into one canonical format before they enter the model context. Prompts and after-the-fact review do not reliably prevent misinterpretation.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A compliance-review workflow always needs the same four steps: extract clauses, compare policy, assign severity, and generate a report. The team wants inspectable outputs between steps. Which pattern is most appropriate?
options: Dynamic decomposition, because the model can invent subtasks as new findings appear
Prompt chaining, with each step feeding the next as a separate call
A single broad prompt, because the workflow is predictable and bounded
Parallel subagents, because every step can run independently from the source document
questions.rationale: Predictable multi-step workflows with inspectable intermediate artifacts are a good fit for prompt chaining. Dynamic decomposition is better when the next tasks depend on discoveries. Parallel execution is not correct when later steps depend on earlier outputs.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A Claude Code investigation found two plausible refactor strategies from the same baseline analysis. The architect wants both explored independently without copying notes into two unrelated chats. What should they use?
options: --continue, because it always chooses the latest session automatically
A new chat for each branch, with the baseline pasted manually into both
fork_session, creating independent branches from the shared baseline
/compact, because it creates separate resumable branches after summarizing
questions.rationale: fork_session is designed for divergent exploration from a shared baseline. Manual copying risks omissions, while --continue resumes rather than branches. Compaction reduces context; it does not create independent investigation branches.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator asks three subagents to investigate a product recall. The supplier-data subagent times out after collecting two of five regions and returns partial records. The coordinator currently discards its output as failed. What should change?
options: Retry the supplier subagent silently until it returns every region so the next component can decide the final handling path
Proceed with the other two subagents and omit supplier data entirely
Mark the whole recall workflow failed to avoid partial conclusions
Use the partial results plus structured error context to decide targeted re-delegation
questions.rationale: Partial results are often still useful when paired with structured error metadata. The coordinator can identify which regions are missing and re-delegate only the gap. Silent retries may waste work, while discarding or terminating loses recoverable information.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator has to launch legal, technical, and financial review subagents for independent checks. Its current implementation waits for each Task call to complete before issuing the next. What is the better pattern?
options: Emit all three Task tool calls in a single coordinator response
Add parallel=true to each sequential Task call payload
Use batch processing so the subagents can share one result channel
Give every subagent the same tools and let them divide the work
questions.rationale: Parallel subagent spawning is triggered when the coordinator emits multiple Task tool calls in one response. A parallel flag is not the core mechanism. Batch processing and broad tool access solve different problems and do not preserve coordinator-managed orchestration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A hotel support agent receives: “My room key stopped working, the invoice has a duplicate parking charge, and I need late checkout.” It resolves the key issue and ignores the rest. What design change addresses this?
options: Ask guests to file separate tickets for billing, access, and checkout issues
Decompose the message into distinct concerns and investigate them in parallel
Route the entire message to the billing specialist because money is involved
Add a final prompt reminder saying to check for unresolved concerns without adding a deterministic validation boundary
questions.rationale: The agent needs to identify multiple concerns as separate work items, not treat the first issue as the whole request. Parallel investigation lets each concern reach the right tools or specialist and then be synthesized into one reply. Asking for new tickets or relying on a reminder weakens the user experience and reliability.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A procurement agent may create purchase orders up to $10,000 but must route larger amounts for approval. Prompt instructions reduced violations but did not eliminate them. What is the right enforcement point?
options: A nightly audit that reverses unauthorized purchase orders over the limit
A longer policy section in CLAUDE.md with examples of valid purchases
A PreToolUse hook that blocks create_purchase_order above the threshold
A cost-estimation subagent that reviews purchase orders after creation
questions.rationale: A PreToolUse hook blocks the action before it reaches the backend, giving a deterministic control. Audits and post-hoc review catch violations after damage may occur. Prompt examples can guide behavior but cannot guarantee policy compliance.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: After a warehouse agent calls reserve_slot, the developer appends the result as plain assistant text: “slot reserved.” Claude then calls reserve_slot again because it cannot correlate the result. What should the harness send?
options: An assistant message containing the raw JSON returned by reserve_slot
A system message updating inventory state for the rest of the conversation
A hidden developer note saying the previous tool already completed and relying on the current prompt guidance for exceptions
A user message containing a tool_result block with the matching tool_use_id
questions.rationale: Tool results need to be returned as structured tool_result blocks correlated to the original tool_use_id. Plain assistant text loses the structured link Claude expects in the agentic loop. System messages or hidden notes are not the standard tool-result return path.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A field-service assistant handles “replace printer toner” tickets and rare “factory line intermittently shuts down after firmware rollout” incidents. The same exhaustive 9-step diagnostic pipeline runs for both. What architectural property is being sacrificed?
options: Adaptive depth, because simple and complex work receive the same decomposition
Predictability, because simple tickets should always use the same checklist
Least privilege, because both workflows use identical diagnostic tools so the next component can decide the final handling path
Attribution, because all findings flow through one coordinator summary
questions.rationale: The pipeline is predictable, but it wastes effort by treating all tickets as equally complex. Adaptive decomposition would keep simple cases shallow while expanding investigation for multi-system incidents. Least privilege and attribution may matter elsewhere, but the stated failure is depth calibration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A Claude Code session analyzed a payment module on Monday. On Wednesday, another team rewrote the retry layer outside that session. What is most reliable before asking for new recommendations?
options: Resume the Monday session and trust its earlier tool results for context
Start fresh with a structured summary plus the current changed files
Use --continue so Claude automatically picks up changed files from disk
Fork the Monday session and ask both branches to compare suggestions
questions.rationale: When prior tool results are stale, a fresh session with a structured summary and current file state is safer. Resuming preserves old context that can bias recommendations toward code that no longer exists. Forking stale context creates two stale branches rather than a reliable baseline.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team lets research subagents message each other directly to resolve disagreements before reporting to the coordinator. Debugging later shows unobserved decisions and inconsistent recovery. What hub-and-spoke rule was violated?
options: Every subagent should inherit the coordinator conversation history
The synthesis agent should own all error handling and retry policy
All inter-subagent communication should route through the coordinator
Subagents should run sequentially whenever conflicts are possible without adding a deterministic validation boundary
questions.rationale: In a hub-and-spoke architecture, the coordinator manages routing, error handling, and observability. Direct subagent communication hides decisions from the component responsible for orchestration. Context inheritance and sequential execution are not the core requirement.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A medical intake agent escalates a policy exception to a nurse but sends only the patient’s last message. The nurse repeats screening questions already answered and misses a medication constraint. What should the handoff include?
options: Only the complete transcript, so the nurse can reconstruct the case independently
A confidence score explaining why the agent decided not to continue autonomously
A short note saying the request is complicated and needs clinical judgment while leaving the existing workflow boundaries unchanged
Customer details, root cause, attempted steps, constraints, and recommended action
questions.rationale: A structured handoff should summarize the operationally important state, not force the human to re-read or infer it. Key details include identity, root cause, prior attempts, constraints, and next recommendation. A transcript alone is inefficient, and confidence without evidence is not actionable.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A retail agent confuses lookup_sku and find_product because both descriptions say “gets product information.” What is the most effective first fix?
options: Expand descriptions with inputs, outputs, examples, and when-not-to-use boundaries
Rename both tools to shorter names that are easier for the model to read
Force lookup_sku whenever the user message contains any number and relying on the current prompt guidance for exceptions
Wrap both calls inside one generic product_router tool with natural-language input
questions.rationale: Tool descriptions are the primary routing signal for similar tools. Clear boundaries, expected identifiers, and examples help Claude select the right tool without brittle keyword rules. A generic router may move the ambiguity rather than solve it.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A policy_lookup MCP tool returns “failed” for invalid policy IDs, permission denials, and service timeouts. The agent retries all failures three times, annoying users. What should the tool return?
options: A longer natural-language paragraph explaining the backend failure in detail
Structured error metadata with category, retryability, and a user-facing message
A success response with an empty result whenever the tool cannot return data
A stack trace so the model can infer whether retrying is appropriate so the next component can decide the final handling path
questions.rationale: The agent needs machine-readable error categories and retryability to choose recovery behavior. Timeouts differ from validation or permission errors, so one generic failure produces wasted retries. Empty success responses and stack traces blur the distinction the coordinator needs.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A synthesis agent occasionally launches fresh web searches even though its job is to merge already vetted research. It has access to the same 14 tools as the research agents. What should change?
options: Give the synthesis agent stronger instructions to avoid searching unless necessary
Use a lower effort setting so the agent is less likely to take extra actions
Restrict it to synthesis tools and perhaps a narrow verify_fact helper
Remove all tools from every agent and route all actions through the coordinator
questions.rationale: Agents should receive tools aligned to their role. A synthesis agent can have a scoped verify_fact helper for common checks, but broad research access invites role leakage. Removing all tools is too extreme and would prevent useful specialized work.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team wants everyone in a repo to use the same Jira MCP server while each developer can keep personal prototype servers private. Where should the configurations live?
options: Team server in CLAUDE.md; personal servers in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
All servers in .mcp.json with comments marking personal sections
All servers in environment variables without checked-in configuration
Team server in .mcp.json; personal servers in ~/.claude.json
questions.rationale: Project-scoped MCP servers belong in .mcp.json so the team can share them through version control. Personal experimental servers belong in user-level ~/.claude.json. CLAUDE.md is for instructions, not MCP server configuration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer needs to find every call site of calculateRisk across a TypeScript monorepo, then inspect the most relevant files. Which Claude Code tool sequence is best?
options: Grep for calculateRisk, then Read the files containing relevant matches
Glob for every .ts file, then Read all matches before searching names
Bash find over the repository, then Write a generated index file while leaving the existing workflow boundaries unchanged
Edit each suspected file and rely on failures to reveal non-matches
questions.rationale: Grep searches file contents and is the correct first step for call sites. Read should follow on relevant files to understand context. Glob finds path patterns, not function references, and Write/Edit are inappropriate for discovery.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A single analyze_document tool extracts tables, summarizes prose, checks citations, and verifies claims. In production, Claude calls it for everything and downstream outputs vary wildly. What redesign improves reliability?
options: Keep the generic tool but add a very long description covering every capability
Split it into purpose-specific tools with narrow contracts and clear outputs
Add a system prompt saying analyze_document has four separate internal modes
Force analyze_document first, then ask Claude to decide which mode was used
questions.rationale: A generic multi-purpose tool creates unclear routing and output expectations. Splitting it into focused tools like extract_tables, summarize_section, and verify_claim gives Claude clearer action boundaries. Long descriptions or modes preserve the original ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A candidate-search tool finds no matching records for a valid query and returns isError=true. The agent apologizes for a system outage and escalates. What should the tool do instead?
options: Return a transient error so the agent retries with broader criteria
Return permission denied because no user data can be shown
Return success with an empty results array and useful query metadata
Return a generic failure and let the coordinator decide what happened
questions.rationale: No matches is a valid business result, not a tool failure. Returning success with an empty result lets the agent ask for more criteria or explain that no records matched. Marking it as an error triggers the wrong recovery behavior.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A document pipeline must always call extract_metadata first, then allow Claude to choose enrichment tools based on the metadata. Which tool_choice sequence fits?
options: Use auto for every request and put the required sequence in the system prompt
Use any on the first request, then forced tool selection for enrichment
Use none first so Claude can plan, then any for all later requests
Force extract_metadata first, then switch tool_choice to auto
questions.rationale: Forced tool selection guarantees the specific first tool. After metadata exists, auto lets Claude reason about which enrichment tools are needed. any would guarantee a tool call but not necessarily the right first tool.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A support agent burns six calls per case just discovering which help-center articles exist before reading one. The article set changes weekly, but the agent only needs visibility into titles and paths. What MCP design helps?
options: Expose a resource catalog of article paths and metadata for discovery
Preload every article body into the system prompt at session start
Create a single search_all_articles tool that always returns full text
Hardcode current article titles into the tool descriptions each release
questions.rationale: MCP resources are well suited for discoverable catalogs such as documentation hierarchies. They let the agent see what exists before deciding which retrieval action is necessary. Preloading full articles or hardcoding titles wastes context and quickly becomes stale.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude Code tries to Edit a config file, but the anchor text appears in four service blocks and the edit fails. What is the safest fallback?
options: Run a shell substitution against the first match and inspect the diff later
Use Read to load the full file, modify the intended block, then Write it back
Retry Edit with the same text until Claude selects the intended block
Delete duplicate blocks first so the Edit anchor becomes unique while leaving the existing workflow boundaries unchanged
questions.rationale: When Edit cannot identify a unique anchor, Read plus Write gives full control over the exact modified content. Blind shell substitution or repeated Edit attempts can change the wrong block. Deleting duplicates changes unrelated semantics.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A project-level MCP server needs a GitHub token, but the team does not want secrets committed. What should .mcp.json contain?
options: The shared token encrypted with a comment explaining how to decrypt it
A reference to CLAUDE.md where every developer stores their token
A placeholder that uses environment variable expansion such as ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
A personal token copied into the repo by each developer after cloning
questions.rationale: Project configuration can reference environment variables so the file is shareable without containing secret values. Each developer or CI environment provides the token locally. Storing tokens in CLAUDE.md or the repo defeats the purpose.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A new teammate does not get the team’s test-generation instructions. They are stored in the lead developer’s ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. What is wrong?
options: Test-generation instructions must live only inside slash commands
Claude Code ignores user-level memory during repository sessions
The /memory command must be run before every test task manually
User-level memory is not shared through the project repository
questions.rationale: User-level CLAUDE.md affects only that developer. Team standards should live at the project or directory level so they are version-controlled. Slash commands and /memory can help workflows, but they do not make private memory shared.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A security audit workflow produces long exploration logs and should not pollute the main conversation. Developers should invoke it on demand from the repo. Which packaging is best?
options: A project skill with context: fork and scoped allowed-tools
A root CLAUDE.md section containing the full audit checklist and all examples
A user-level slash command each developer copies into their home directory
A path-specific rule that loads whenever any source file is opened
questions.rationale: A skill is appropriate for an on-demand reusable workflow, and context: fork isolates verbose output. allowed-tools can restrict what the audit may do. CLAUDE.md or path rules would load more often than necessary, and user-level commands are not shared by the repo.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A monorepo has test files under apps, packages, and services. The team wants mocking rules loaded only when editing test files. What should they use?
options: Directory-level CLAUDE.md files copied into every __tests__ directory
.claude/rules/ with YAML paths like **/*.test.ts and **/__tests__/**
A root CLAUDE.md section that says to apply test rules only when relevant
A /test-rules slash command developers run before touching any test file
questions.rationale: Path-specific rules with glob patterns apply conventions by file path wherever the files live. That avoids duplicating directory-level files and keeps irrelevant rules out of non-test sessions. Manual slash commands rely on developers remembering to invoke them.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer needs to add a missing null check to one function named parseWebhookTimestamp. The failing test points to the exact file and branch. Which mode is appropriate?
options: Plan mode, because every code change should be designed before execution
Explore subagent, because it preserves context better than direct edits
Direct execution, because the task is simple and well scoped
Forked session, because bug fixes should compare several strategies
questions.rationale: Direct execution is appropriate for a small, clear change with known location and behavior. Plan mode is more useful for architectural or multi-file decisions. Forking and exploration add overhead without solving a stated uncertainty.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude keeps generating migration scripts that mishandle null legacy values despite prose instructions. What feedback should the developer provide?
options: A shorter instruction saying null handling is the highest priority
A request to “think harder” before writing the migration code
A lower temperature setting and no examples to avoid overfitting
Concrete input/output examples covering nulls and expected transformed rows
questions.rationale: Concrete examples are the strongest way to communicate expected transformations when prose is interpreted inconsistently. They show how edge cases should map through the migration. Priority language and generic “think harder” prompts do not define the target behavior precisely.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A GitHub Actions job running Claude Code for PR feedback hangs because it waits for interactive input. What flag addresses this?
options: -p or --print
--daemon
--watch=false
--headless-ci
questions.rationale: The -p/--print mode is used for non-interactive Claude Code execution in scripted or CI contexts. It processes the prompt and exits instead of waiting in a chat loop. The other flags are not the relevant CI mechanism here.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A root CLAUDE.md has grown to 900 lines. Claude follows early style rules but misses deployment and security conventions near the end. What should the team do?
options: Increase max_tokens so Claude has more room to read the memory file
Split core rules into concise memory, @import details, and path-scoped rule files
Move all rules into one JSON file so tokenization is more compact
Keep the file unchanged and add a reminder at the bottom to read everything
questions.rationale: A large always-loaded file can dilute attention and waste context. Keeping root memory concise, importing detailed sections, and using path-scoped rules loads relevant guidance when needed. max_tokens controls output length, not whether long instructions are attended to.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A project skill /release-notes accepts a version string like 2.4.1. Which SKILL.md mechanism should reference the provided argument?
options: a required-params frontmatter array with automatic variable binding
an input_schema property that maps version to a JSON field
$ARGUMENTS or positional variables such as $1 inside the skill content
a CLAUDE_ARGS environment variable created by Claude Code
questions.rationale: Skills can use the full argument string via $ARGUMENTS and positional substitutions such as $1. argument-hint can help prompt the user, but it is not a schema-binding system. input_schema is a tool concept, not the basic skill argument mechanism.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Before changing a legacy billing module, a developer wants architecture discovery but wants raw Grep and Read output kept out of the main conversation. What workflow fits?
options: Read all billing files in the main session, then use /compact before coding
Start direct execution and ask Claude to summarize discoveries after every edit
Use a user-level CLAUDE.md note telling Claude not to include long outputs
Use the Explore subagent for discovery, then plan mode for the change approach
questions.rationale: Explore is intended to isolate verbose discovery and return summaries to the main session. Plan mode then supports architectural decisions before implementation. Reading everything in the main thread creates the context pressure the workflow is trying to avoid.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A CI review bot posts malformed markdown because Claude sometimes returns prose, sometimes JSON, and sometimes bullet lists. What Claude Code flags should the job use?
options: -p with --output-format json and --json-schema for machine-parseable findings
--watch with a markdown template stored in CLAUDE.md
--resume with the pull request number as the session name
--interactive=false with a request to return JSON only
questions.rationale: CI systems should use non-interactive execution with structured output flags and a schema. This makes downstream posting deterministic. Prompting for JSON alone is weaker than using the dedicated output-format and schema options.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer asks Claude to implement cache invalidation for a domain they barely understand. The first implementation misses tenant isolation and rollback behavior. What refinement pattern would have helped before coding?
options: Use direct execution so implementation details expose missing requirements quickly
Ask Claude to interview the developer about assumptions and edge cases first
Disable project memory to avoid over-constraining the design conversation
Ask Claude to produce three versions and choose the shortest implementation
questions.rationale: The interview pattern is useful when requirements are under-specified and the developer may not know what considerations matter. It surfaces constraints before implementation. Direct execution or choosing the shortest version risks cementing incomplete assumptions.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A Claude PR review runs on every push and repeats the same already-posted findings, causing reviewer fatigue. What should the CI prompt include on reruns?
options: Only the latest diff, because prior comments may bias the model too much
A request to lower severity for repeated comments instead of suppressing them
Prior automated findings, with instructions to report only new or unresolved issues
A unique session identifier so Claude can infer which comments were posted
questions.rationale: Prior findings give Claude the state needed to avoid duplicate feedback and focus on new or still-unresolved issues. A session identifier alone does not provide the previous comments. Lowering severity still leaves duplicate noise in the pull request.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A code review prompt says “be conservative,” but it still flags harmless local style choices as defects. What prompt change is most useful?
options: Ask Claude to include only findings where it feels at least 90% confident
Increase the context window so the model can inspect more surrounding code
Ask for fewer findings so only the most important ones remain
Define explicit report/skip criteria with concrete examples for each category
questions.rationale: Specific criteria outperform vague caution language. Examples of reportable and non-reportable findings help the model distinguish real defects from style preferences. Self-reported confidence and arbitrary caps do not teach the judgment boundary.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An extraction prompt handles formal invoices well but fails on handwritten delivery notes with informal quantities like “two pallets plus spare box.” What is the best prompt improvement?
options: Provide 2-4 examples showing correct extraction from varied informal formats
Add a warning that informal notes are high risk and should be skipped
Make every quantity field required so Claude must produce structured values
Retry the same prompt until one output happens to include quantities
questions.rationale: Few-shot examples demonstrate the desired treatment of ambiguous and varied source formats. They help the model generalize beyond the formal invoice layout. Required fields can increase fabrication, and blind retry does not address the missing pattern.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A triage service must always return one JSON object with status, severity, and routing fields. It is not trying to call a backend tool. Which mechanism best fits response-level structure?
options: Plain prompt instructions with a fenced JSON template
output_config.format using a JSON schema with strict mode
Post-processing that reparses markdown and fills missing fields
A tool schema plus auto tool_choice so Claude may call it
questions.rationale: For whole-response JSON, response-level structured output with a JSON schema is the direct fit. Tool schemas are strong when the structure is a tool input, but auto tool_choice may return text. Post-processing catches problems after they occur rather than preventing them.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An invoice extractor retries twice after validation says line items total $428 but the printed total is $462. The image clearly shows those numbers; neither is a parsing mistake. What should happen next?
options: Retry with a higher effort setting so arithmetic has more room to converge
Force the printed total to match the calculated total during post-processing
Flag a source-document discrepancy and route or annotate for review
Simplify the schema by dropping calculated_total from the output contract
questions.rationale: Retries help when the model made a structural or extraction error, not when the source itself contains a conflict. The correct behavior is to preserve the discrepancy and route or annotate it. Forcing a match hides evidence, and removing validation weakens quality control.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A firm wants Claude to process 40,000 archived supplier reports over the weekend for a Monday dashboard. The job is non-blocking and results can arrive later. What API strategy fits?
options: Real-time synchronous calls from the dashboard page on Monday morning
Claude Code interactive mode with a long-running terminal session
A single request containing every report to maximize context sharing
Message Batches API with custom_id values for correlating results
questions.rationale: Batch processing fits large, latency-tolerant workloads and can correlate responses using custom IDs. Synchronous calls are more appropriate for blocking user workflows. One giant request would exceed practical context and remove per-document recoverability.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A generator writes a data-access patch and then reviews it in the same session. The review misses a subtle query bug that a separate reviewer catches. What explains the difference?
options: A separate review instance avoids the generator’s reasoning context bias
The same session lacks enough context to understand the generated code
The generator should have used a lower temperature during review
Reviewing after generation requires batch processing instead of chat
questions.rationale: Self-review is weaker because the session retains the reasoning context that produced the artifact. An independent reviewer is more likely to question assumptions and catch subtle issues. Temperature and batch processing do not directly solve context contamination.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A review prompt mixes security, documentation, and accessibility rules in paragraphs. Claude applies accessibility rules to backend files and ignores security criteria. What structure helps?
options: Reduce the prompt to one paragraph so nothing is overlooked
Use XML-style sections separating concern areas and criteria
Ask Claude to infer which rules apply from the file name
Move all criteria into option text in the generated findings
questions.rationale: Structured sections make rule groups and applicability easier to parse. XML-style tags can reduce accidental blending of unrelated criteria. Shorter prose or inferred applicability does not provide the same explicit boundaries.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A contract extractor fabricates governing_law for draft agreements where the clause is absent. What schema design change helps?
options: Make governing_law required and add “unknown” as a default string
Use a post-processor to delete suspicious governing_law values
Make governing_law nullable and instruct null when absent from the source
Ask Claude to search its training knowledge for the likely jurisdiction
questions.rationale: Nullable fields give the model a valid way to represent missing source information. Required strings pressure the model to fill something even when the document lacks it. Post-processing and outside knowledge do not solve the extraction contract.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A JSON extraction fails validation because invoice_date is “next Friday” instead of ISO 8601. The source includes a clear document date. What should the retry include?
options: Only the validation error, so the model focuses on the failed field
A request to ignore date fields in the next attempt
A generic instruction to produce cleaner JSON next time
The original document, failed extraction, and the specific validation error
questions.rationale: A retry-with-feedback loop should include the source, the failed output, and the precise validation error. That gives Claude enough context to correct the field without inventing values. A generic instruction or dropping the field weakens the extraction goal.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team wants to use batch requests for a workflow where Claude must call a lookup tool, receive its result, and then decide whether to call a second tool. Why is this a poor fit?
options: Batch requests cannot perform multi-turn tool calling inside one request
Batch processing costs more than synchronous calls for multi-step tasks
Batch processing cannot return JSON schema-constrained outputs
Batch jobs require all tool calls to be forced before submission
questions.rationale: Batch processing is for independent requests and is not designed for interactive mid-request tool execution and result return. Multi-turn tool loops belong in a synchronous harness. The issue is not JSON output or cost; it is the need for turn-by-turn tool orchestration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A single-pass review of a 19-file PR misses API mismatches between a service and its client while over-focusing on one large file. What review architecture is stronger?
options: A single larger prompt that places the most complex file first
Per-file local reviews followed by a separate cross-file integration pass
One reviewer with instructions to allocate equal attention to every file
Only a cross-file pass, because local issues are already tested by CI
questions.rationale: Multi-pass review reduces attention dilution. Local passes inspect each file deeply, and an integration pass catches cross-file contract issues. A larger monolithic prompt still risks uneven attention and contradictory findings.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A review bot repeatedly flags intentional test doubles as “mocking production behavior” and developers dismiss those comments. Which feedback-loop field would help improve the prompt systematically?
options: A global confidence score averaged across all findings
A summary sentence saying whether the finding seemed important
A detected_pattern field capturing the construct that triggered each finding
A boolean stating whether the reviewer liked the code style
questions.rationale: Capturing detected_pattern enables analysis of which constructs generate dismissed findings. The team can then add examples or criteria for those exact patterns. A global confidence score or vague summary is too coarse to guide prompt repair.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A long support chat is compacted and later the agent remembers “a refund was discussed” but loses the exact $187 amount and promised date. What pattern prevents this?
options: Increase max_tokens so the prior messages are never summarized
Ask the customer to restate all important details after compaction
Keep every raw tool result in context until the case closes
Extract transactional facts into a persistent case-facts block
questions.rationale: Critical amounts, dates, IDs, and commitments should be stored in a persistent structured layer. That layer survives summarization better than relying on conversational memory. More raw context increases pressure and still may lose exact values during compaction.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A university records agent finds two students named Alex Rivera, one in Biology and one in Finance. The user only provided the name and asks to change an address. What should the agent do?
options: Ask for an additional identifier before taking account-specific action
Choose the most recently active record and note that it can be corrected later
Update both records with a pending flag until the user clarifies
Use the user’s IP location to infer the most likely campus department
questions.rationale: Multiple matches require clarification before consequential action. Heuristics like recency or IP can select the wrong person and create privacy or operational harm. Updating both records is worse because it spreads the error.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A document-analysis subagent returns no citations because the repository permission token expired. The coordinator treats it as “no relevant documents found.” What distinction was lost?
options: A low-confidence synthesis versus a high-confidence synthesis
A valid empty result versus an access failure needing recovery
A formatting failure versus a schema validation failure
A prompt-routing decision versus a tool-selection decision
questions.rationale: No matches and access failures mean very different things. A permission failure should trigger recovery, fallback, or escalation, while a valid empty result may support a conclusion. Treating both as empty results hides the real coverage gap.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)
