questions.text: During a 3-hour codebase investigation, Claude starts saying “typical controller pattern” instead of naming the files it inspected earlier. What practice helps preserve discovered facts?
options: Rely on --resume because it restores all prior reasoning perfectly
Keep asking Claude to remember the exact files in natural language
Maintain a scratchpad file with findings, file paths, and open questions
Raise output length so responses include more investigation history
questions.rationale: Scratchpad files externalize durable investigation state outside the context window. They can be re-read after compaction or a fresh session. Resuming chat history alone can preserve stale or degraded context rather than reliable structured facts.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A legal extraction system reports 96% overall accuracy. A manual audit finds assignment clauses are 99% accurate but indemnity caps are 71%. What evaluation change is needed?
options: Lower the overall target so difficult fields do not dominate the score
Increase the total sample size while keeping one global accuracy metric
Route only low-confidence records to audit and skip high-confidence ones
Use stratified measurement by document type and field segment
questions.rationale: Aggregate accuracy can hide failures in specific document-field segments. Stratified evaluation exposes weak slices like indemnity caps even when the global score looks strong. Increasing one global sample or lowering standards does not reveal or fix segment-specific risk.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A climate report merges two credible sources: one says 2023 emissions, the other says 2024 preliminary emissions. The synthesis states a single number without dates. What should the system require?
options: Preserve claim-source mappings with dates and annotate the temporal difference
Pick the newer value automatically whenever two statistics conflict
Average credible values to avoid favoring one source too strongly
Remove both statistics so the final report avoids contested numbers
questions.rationale: Temporal metadata can explain differences that look like conflicts. Structured claim-source mappings with dates let the report distinguish 2023 measured data from 2024 preliminary data. Averaging or picking blindly destroys provenance and may mislead readers.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A customer says, “I know you may be able to fix it, but I want a human manager now.” The agent has more troubleshooting steps available. What should it do?
options: Continue troubleshooting because the issue might still be easy to resolve
Honor the explicit human request and provide a structured handoff
Ask the customer to try one more step before escalation
Escalate only if sentiment analysis confirms high frustration
questions.rationale: An explicit request for a human is a hard escalation trigger. The agent should not delay escalation just because it might still resolve the issue. Sentiment is an unreliable proxy when the user has already stated a preference.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator manages five code-exploration agents. After a crash, the team can recover chat history but not which agent inspected which subsystem or which files remain unresolved. What state design helps?
options: The coordinator asks every agent to repeat its entire investigation after any crash
All agents append raw terminal output to one shared transcript file
Each agent exports structured state to known paths, and the coordinator loads a manifest on resume
The system disables subagents for any workflow that might need recovery
questions.rationale: Structured state exports and a coordinator manifest make crash recovery explicit and inspectable. Repeating all work wastes time, while raw transcripts are hard to merge and summarize reliably. Disabling subagents avoids the recovery problem by losing the benefits of decomposition.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A loan-document extractor auto-approves any field with model confidence above 0.90. Later, collateral_value at 0.94 is wrong 18% of the time, while borrower_name at 0.88 is almost always right. What should change?
options: Use one higher global threshold, such as 0.97, for every extracted field
Trust confidence only for simple text fields and ignore it for numeric fields
Remove confidence scores and route every extraction to manual review
Calibrate thresholds per document type and field using labeled validation data
questions.rationale: Raw model confidence is only a signal until calibrated against labeled outcomes. Thresholds should vary by field and document type because errors are not distributed evenly. A single global threshold wastes review capacity and may still miss overconfident weak fields.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A logistics agent receives a Claude response with stop_reason set to tool_use and two tool requests: check_inventory and estimate_delivery. The developer wants to treat the response as final because assistant text is also present. What should the loop do?
options: Run the tools, return matching tool_result blocks, then continue.
End the loop because any assistant text means Claude has finished.
Retry the request with a larger max_tokens value before tools.
Ask the user to choose which tool result should be trusted.
questions.rationale: The loop continues when stop_reason is tool_use, even if assistant text is also present. The application should execute the tool calls, return correlated tool_result blocks, and continue until a terminal stop reason appears.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A clinical research coordinator delegates literature search and trial-registry analysis to separate subagents. The synthesis agent omits the registry findings even though the coordinator received them. What is the most likely design flaw?
options: The registry subagent should write results into global memory.
The coordinator failed to include registry findings in the synthesis task.
The synthesis agent needs direct trial-registry tool access.
The coordinator should increase temperature for final synthesis.
questions.rationale: Subagents do not automatically inherit each other's context or the coordinator's history. The coordinator must explicitly pass prior findings into the synthesis prompt.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A warranty agent occasionally authorizes replacements before verifying serial-number ownership. Prompt reminders reduced the error from 9% to 3%, but the business requires zero unauthorized replacements. What should be added?
options: A higher-effort model for all warranty conversations.
More examples showing serial-number checks before replacements.
A pre-tool gate blocking replacement until ownership is verified.
A nightly report listing replacements missing verification.
questions.rationale: The requirement is deterministic compliance, so a programmatic precondition is needed before the sensitive action. More prompting, stronger models, or audits still leave a non-zero chance of violation or detect the issue too late.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator must compare legal, technical, and cost implications of a vendor migration. Each analysis can begin from the same baseline independently. How should the coordinator trigger the work?
options: Call Task once, wait for the result, then call the next specialist.
Let specialists infer the baseline from the coordinator history.
Use Message Batches because all parallel work must be batched.
Emit three Task calls in one response with the baseline in each prompt.
questions.rationale: Parallel subagent spawning is done by emitting multiple Task tool calls in a single coordinator response. Each subagent needs the baseline explicitly because contexts are isolated.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A procurement assistant handles both simple price checks and complex supplier-risk investigations. A fixed 11-step workflow gives consistent output but triples latency for simple requests. What architecture best preserves quality without wasting work?
options: Use adaptive decomposition that expands only when findings require it.
Run the full workflow only when confidence is below a threshold.
Move supplier-risk checks into a separate always-on background job.
Ask users to classify their request before the agent begins.
questions.rationale: Variable-complexity work is a fit for adaptive decomposition. Simple cases can resolve quickly, while complex investigations spawn deeper subtasks based on intermediate findings.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A travel support agent calls airline, hotel, and payment MCP tools. Dates return as local strings, ISO timestamps, and Unix seconds, causing bad cancellation-window comparisons. Where should normalization occur?
options: In a user-facing apology when date conflicts are detected.
In a PostToolUse hook before Claude reasons over results.
In the system prompt as a reminder to convert every date.
In a final report generator after all decisions are made.
questions.rationale: PostToolUse hooks can transform heterogeneous tool results before the model processes them. Prompt reminders and final formatting do not reliably prevent reasoning over inconsistent date formats.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Three research agents studying autonomous warehouses all focus on robotics vendors and miss labor policy, safety compliance, and integration costs. The agents followed their assigned tasks well. What failed?
options: The subagents needed larger context windows for broader recall.
The synthesis agent should have searched for missing topics itself.
The coordinator under-scoped the research decomposition.
The report generator should add generic background sections.
questions.rationale: When subagents execute their assigned work but the final answer has coverage gaps, the coordinator's decomposition is usually too narrow. The fix is to partition the research space more completely before delegation.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A telecom agent receives: 'My bill doubled, my roaming failed, and I want to cancel.' It resolves billing first, then restarts customer lookup for roaming and cancellation. What improves handling?
options: Add a checkpoint after each concern to confirm partial resolution.
Require the customer to open three separate support tickets.
Build one generic resolve_customer_issue tool for all concerns.
Decompose concerns, share customer context, investigate in parallel.
questions.rationale: Multi-concern requests should be decomposed into distinct items while reusing shared context. Independent investigations can run in parallel and then be synthesized into one response.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: After a week, a Claude Code session is resumed for a migration. Several files were renamed and rewritten outside the session. Claude confidently references old paths from earlier tool calls. What is the safest continuation pattern?
options: Start fresh with a summary and current code state.
Fork the old session before making any new edits.
Resume and ask Claude to trust only newly read files.
Continue normally because resumed sessions refresh files.
questions.rationale: When prior tool results are stale, a fresh session with structured current-state context is safer than resuming contaminated context. Forking or continuing preserves the stale baseline.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two subagents in a compliance review need to compare their findings. The developer lets them message each other directly to save coordinator tokens. What architectural property is weakened?
options: The ability to use structured JSON outputs at all.
Centralized observability and controlled error handling.
The coordinator's access to built-in file tools.
The model's ability to call multiple tools in parallel.
questions.rationale: In the hub-and-spoke pattern, communication flows through the coordinator for observability, routing, and consistent error handling. Direct subagent communication weakens that control.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A claims agent must not approve payouts above $2,000 without adjuster review. The model sometimes approves $2,500 after a persuasive customer message. Which implementation is most reliable?
options: A PostToolUse hook that reverses oversized approvals.
A prompt rule stating the payout threshold clearly.
A PreToolUse hook that denies the approval call.
A dashboard that highlights oversized approvals later.
questions.rationale: A PreToolUse hook blocks the sensitive action before it executes. Post-hoc reversal, prompt-only guidance, and later dashboards are weaker for guaranteed policy enforcement.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A coordinator passes raw web excerpts, page metadata, and document notes to synthesis as one long paragraph. Citations are lost and conflicting dates are blended. What handoff format is better?
options: A shorter natural-language summary without source details.
A final answer draft that synthesis only polishes.
A raw dump of every page to avoid summary loss.
A structured claim list with source and metadata fields.
questions.rationale: Structured handoffs preserve provenance by separating claims from metadata such as source, page, and date. Plain summaries, raw dumps, and preselected drafts risk attribution loss or hidden conflict resolution.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A release gate must always perform dependency license review, vulnerability scan review, test failure triage, and final decision in that order. Intermediate outputs must be auditable. What pattern fits?
options: Prompt chaining with separate ordered stages.
Adaptive decomposition with no fixed sequence.
One broad review prompt with numbered steps.
Parallel execution of all stages at once.
questions.rationale: A predictable ordered workflow with auditable intermediate outputs is a good fit for prompt chaining. Adaptive or parallel designs are less appropriate when the sequence is required.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer wants to compare two database migration strategies from the same codebase analysis baseline without cross-contaminating the reasoning. What feature best supports this?
options: Use one session with headings for each strategy.
Use fork_session from the shared baseline.
Start unrelated sessions with copied notes.
Use --continue after each strategy branch.
questions.rationale: fork_session creates independent branches from a shared analysis baseline. Separate unrelated sessions require manual copying, while one session risks contamination.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A support agent escalates a complex mortgage case by sending only the last customer message. Human reviewers repeatedly redo the same investigation. What should the escalation include?
options: Only a confidence score and the full transcript link.
A request that the customer restate the issue to the reviewer.
A structured summary of facts, root cause, attempts, and next actions.
A raw log of all tool calls sorted by execution time.
questions.rationale: Human handoff should be structured and actionable: relevant customer facts, root cause, steps tried, and recommended next actions. Raw logs or a last message force reviewers to reconstruct context.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer returns tool results in a user message after a paragraph explaining what the tool did. The API rejects the message. What formatting rule was violated?
options: All tool results must be converted into plain natural language.
Tool results must be sent only inside assistant role messages.
The original tool_use block must be repeated with the result.
tool_result blocks must appear before text blocks in that message.
questions.rationale: When a user message includes tool_result blocks, they must come before any text blocks. Tool results are not assistant messages and should be correlated structurally, not as plain prose.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An agent confuses crm_find_customer and crm_get_customer because both descriptions say 'gets customer information.' What is the best first fix?
options: Add clear descriptions with inputs and use boundaries.
Force tools using keywords from the user message.
Increase model effort for customer-support turns.
Merge both tools into one customer tool.
questions.rationale: Tool descriptions are the primary mechanism for selection. Similar tools need distinct names, expected inputs, outputs, and boundary guidance.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A payment MCP tool returns 'failed' for card decline, permission denial, and gateway timeout. The agent retries every failure. What should the tool return?
options: A longer human-readable error paragraph.
Structured error category and retryability metadata.
A success response with empty payment details.
Only the provider's raw HTTP status code.
questions.rationale: The agent needs machine-readable errorCategory and isRetryable information to distinguish validation, business, permission, and transient failures. Generic text or raw codes are not enough.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A report-writing subagent sometimes calls web_search even though research is supposed to be complete. This causes uncited late additions. What should you change?
options: Raise the writer's effort level so it follows instructions better.
Tell the writer to avoid web_search unless absolutely needed.
Give the writer only report-generation tools and routed verification.
Let the writer search freely and dedupe sources afterward.
questions.rationale: Agents should receive only tools needed for their role. Scoped tool access prevents role leakage and late uncoordinated research.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A documentation agent burns many calls searching only to discover which product manuals exist. What MCP feature reduces that exploratory work?
options: More granular search tools for each manual type.
A larger context window for search results.
Forced tool_choice on the search tool.
MCP resources exposing a manual catalog.
questions.rationale: MCP resources can expose discoverable catalogs or hierarchies. This lets the model see available content without exploratory search calls.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude Code needs to find every file path matching **/*.migration.sql. Which built-in tool is most appropriate?
options: Glob, because it matches file paths.
Grep, because it searches repository contents.
Read, because it loads file text safely.
Edit, because it can locate SQL anchors.
questions.rationale: Glob is for file path patterns. Grep searches file contents, while Read and Edit operate on specific files.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Edit fails because the selected snippet appears in six places. The file is small and must be changed safely. What is the recommended fallback?
options: Run sed to replace the first matching occurrence.
Use Read, modify full content, then Write.
Retry Edit with the same anchor text.
Ask the user to edit the file manually.
questions.rationale: When Edit lacks a unique anchor, Read plus Write gives full-file control. Blind sed or repeated Edit can modify the wrong occurrence.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team wants a shared Linear MCP server but each developer has a personal sandbox server too. Where should the configurations live?
options: Both in project .mcp.json with username filters.
Team in CLAUDE.md, personal in .claude/rules.
Team in .mcp.json, personal in ~/.claude.json.
Both in ~/.claude.json to avoid version-control risk.
questions.rationale: Project-level .mcp.json is for shared team MCP configuration. User-level ~/.claude.json is for personal or experimental servers.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A generic analyze_file tool summarizes, extracts fields, verifies claims, and classifies document type. Claude calls it inconsistently and downstream parsing is brittle. What tool redesign is best?
options: Keep one tool but add a longer multi-page description.
Return prose so parsing is no longer required.
Force analyze_file for every uploaded file.
Split into focused tools with explicit contracts.
questions.rationale: Overly broad tools should be split into purpose-specific tools with clear input/output contracts. A longer description may not fix conflicting purposes.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A policy lookup finds no matching rule for a valid query. The tool currently returns isError=true, causing the agent to retry. What should it return?
options: A successful empty result with no matches.
A transient error so the agent retries later.
A permission error to prevent unsafe actions.
A generic failure with the searched query.
questions.rationale: A valid query with no matches is a successful empty result, not an error. Distinguishing empty success from failure prevents wasted retries.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A document enrichment pipeline must first call extract_metadata, then allow Claude to choose optional enrichment tools. What tool_choice sequence fits?
options: Use any first, then auto for enrichment.
Use forced extract_metadata, then auto.
Use auto first, then forced enrichment.
Use none first, then any for enrichment.
questions.rationale: Forced tool choice guarantees the specific first tool. Switching to auto afterward lets Claude decide which follow-up tools are appropriate.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A project-scoped MCP server needs an API token. The config must be shared, but secrets must not be committed. What pattern should be used?
options: Commit the token in .mcp.json and restrict repo access.
Store the token in root CLAUDE.md.
Use ${TOKEN_NAME} expansion in .mcp.json.
Put the token in .claude/rules/secrets.md.
questions.rationale: .mcp.json can use environment variable expansion so shared configuration stays versioned while each developer provides secrets locally.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team standard for commit messages was added to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md on one engineer's machine. Other engineers do not see it. What is wrong?
options: The /init command must run before every session.
CLAUDE.md cannot contain team workflow instructions.
Commit rules must be stored only in .mcp.json.
User-level memory is personal, not shared by version control.
questions.rationale: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is user-level and personal. Shared team standards belong in project-level CLAUDE.md or related project configuration.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Terraform rules apply to files across infra/, modules/, and examples/. A directory-level CLAUDE.md would duplicate guidance. What should you use?
options: A path-scoped rule with Terraform glob patterns.
A root CLAUDE.md section for all Terraform rules.
A slash command developers run before editing Terraform.
A user-level CLAUDE.md entry for each infra engineer.
questions.rationale: Path-specific rules with glob patterns load only for matching files wherever they appear. This avoids duplicate directory files and irrelevant context.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A developer asks Claude Code to rename a local variable in one function. The file is known and tests are unaffected. Which workflow is best?
options: Plan mode, because every edit needs approval first.
Direct execution, because the change is narrow.
Explore mode, because it isolates discovery output.
Forked sessions, because naming has alternatives.
questions.rationale: Simple, well-scoped changes are suitable for direct execution. Plan mode is more useful for large, uncertain, or architectural changes.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A verbose dependency-audit workflow is useful once per release and should not load during normal coding. Where should it live?
options: Root CLAUDE.md, so release guidance is always present.
A path rule for every package.json file.
A skill invoked on demand for the audit workflow.
User-level memory for the release manager only.
questions.rationale: Task-specific, infrequent, verbose workflows belong in on-demand skills rather than always-loaded memory. This keeps regular sessions lean.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A codebase-mapping skill prints many file summaries and fills the main conversation. Which skill setting addresses this?
options: allowed-tools, so the skill has fewer tools.
argument-hint, so the user supplies a target.
disable-model-invocation, so the skill cannot run.
context: fork, so verbose work runs isolated.
questions.rationale: context: fork runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent context and returns only the useful result. Tool limits and argument hints solve different problems.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A root CLAUDE.md has grown to 900 lines and mixes API, testing, release, and security instructions. Sessions feel overloaded. What is a better organization?
options: Use imports and focused rule files for relevant guidance.
Keep one file so Claude always sees every standard.
Move everything into user-level memory files.
Convert each instruction into a slash command.
questions.rationale: Modular imports and focused rule files reduce irrelevant context while keeping standards maintainable. Slash commands are for manual workflows, not all standing guidance.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A GitHub Action running Claude Code hangs waiting for user input. Which CLI pattern is appropriate?
options: Use /init before the CI job starts.
Use -p or --print for non-interactive mode.
Use /memory to pre-load project files.
Use --resume with the PR number.
questions.rationale: Claude Code should run in non-interactive print mode for CI. Session commands and memory inspection do not make the process headless.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A Dockerized code-review job must ignore developers' local skills, hooks, MCP servers, and memories. The team wants identical behavior on every runner. What should be used?
options: Project CLAUDE.md plus a pinned model version.
A shared resumed session for every pull request.
-p with --bare and explicit API-key auth.
User-level config copied into the Docker image.
questions.rationale: --bare avoids auto-discovered Claude Code configuration, and -p supports non-interactive CI. Explicit API-key auth avoids local OAuth or keychain dependence.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A migration skill needs the migration name inserted into its instructions. What mechanism should the skill use?
options: A required-params frontmatter field.
A temporary environment variable only.
A JSON input_schema in SKILL.md.
$ARGUMENTS with an argument-hint.
questions.rationale: Skills and commands can use argument substitution such as $ARGUMENTS, while argument-hint guides the user. Tool-style input_schema is not the skill argument mechanism.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude Code must replace a homegrown auth layer across frontend, backend, and tests. There are two viable migration approaches and rollback concerns. What should happen first?
options: Use plan mode to compare approaches before editing.
Start direct edits in the backend auth module.
Run the final test suite before reading files.
Create a slash command after the refactor finishes.
questions.rationale: Large multi-file work with architectural tradeoffs is a plan-mode situation. Direct edits before exploration risk choosing a poor approach.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Claude Code is ignoring a convention, and the developer wants to see which memory files are loaded. Which command helps?
options: /status
/memory
/config
/debug
questions.rationale: /memory is used to inspect loaded memory files and troubleshoot configuration behavior.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team wants a reusable prompt for writing release notes. It is short, manually invoked, and does not need isolated context or tool restrictions. What is the simplest fit?
options: A user-level CLAUDE.md release section.
A forked skill with restricted allowed-tools.
A project slash command in .claude/commands.
A project .mcp.json server definition.
questions.rationale: A short manually invoked reusable prompt fits a project-scoped slash command. Skills are better when you need richer behavior, isolation, or tool controls.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A code-review prompt mixes security, style, and documentation rules in prose. Claude applies them inconsistently. What prompt structure helps?
options: Ask Claude to remember the checklist first.
Make one longer paragraph with stronger wording.
Increase output length so all rules fit.
Use XML-style sections for each concern area.
questions.rationale: Clear delimiters or XML-style sections separate rule groups and reduce misinterpretation. Stronger prose alone usually does not fix structural ambiguity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: An automated reviewer flags safe try/catch blocks as missing error handling. General instructions to avoid false positives did not help. What prompt addition is strongest?
options: Few-shot examples of the false-positive pattern.
A higher confidence threshold on every finding.
A request for fewer total findings per file.
A longer generic description of error handling.
questions.rationale: Targeted few-shot examples teach the intended decision boundary for recurring false positives. Generic caution and thresholds are weaker.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Some invoices lack a purchase-order number. The model invents plausible PO numbers when the field is required. What schema pattern helps?
options: Use a string value such as unknown.
Make purchase_order_number nullable.
Remove all required fields from the schema.
Post-process values that look fabricated.
questions.rationale: Nullable fields let Claude state that the source lacks a value. Required strings can pressure the model to invent absent information.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A document service needs the assistant's whole response to be a single JSON object matching a schema. No tool action is being executed. What should be used?
options: Forced tool_use with an extraction tool.
Markdown JSON fences with examples.
output_config json_schema strict mode.
A parser that repairs bad JSON later.
questions.rationale: For whole-response schema guarantees, response-level structured output is the direct fit. Tool-use schemas are for tool input, not necessarily the assistant's final response.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A review must always identify issues, rank severity, and then produce recommendations. In a single response, Claude sometimes skips severity ranking. What enforces the sequence best?
options: Use numbered instructions with MUST on each step.
Add a final self-check after recommendations.
Lower temperature to reduce output variation.
Use separate chained calls for each stage.
questions.rationale: Prompt chaining makes each stage explicit and inspectable. Single-prompt reminders or self-checks remain probabilistic.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A model-generated policy summary is evaluated by the same Claude session that produced it. Scores are consistently generous. What review architecture is better?
options: Use an independent evaluator instance.
Ask the same session to be more skeptical.
Raise temperature during evaluation.
Require a confidence score with each grade.
questions.rationale: The same session retains generation context and is prone to self-review bias. An independent evaluator without that context is more objective.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 16-file security review misses local bugs in dense files and misses cross-file data-flow issues. What review structure is strongest?
options: One high-effort review over every file at once.
Per-file passes followed by integration review.
Only per-file reviews posted independently.
A shorter prompt asking for critical bugs only.
questions.rationale: Per-file passes reduce attention dilution and find local issues. A separate integration pass detects cross-file problems.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A schema enum for ticket_type has billing, technical, and account. Many real tickets are partner-related and get forced into technical. What schema change is best?
options: Remove the enum and use free text.
Keep the enum and add confidence.
Add other plus a detail field.
Create one schema per ticket type.
questions.rationale: The other plus detail pattern preserves controlled categories while capturing unexpected categories for analysis.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A CI prompt asks Claude to 'review this PR thoroughly' and gets style comments plus speculative warnings. What should the prompt specify?
options: A maximum answer length for every review.
A fixed number of comments per changed file.
A friendlier tone for developer trust.
Reportable issue criteria and required evidence.
questions.rationale: CI review prompts should define actionable finding criteria, evidence requirements, and exclusions. Fixed counts or tone changes do not improve relevance.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A workflow needs Claude to call record_review with structured findings so the CI script can process them as tool input. What is the appropriate mechanism?
options: Tool use with a JSON input schema.
Plain JSON in an assistant message.
A markdown table with severity columns.
A natural-language report plus regex parsing.
questions.rationale: When structured data is intended as tool input, tool use with a schema is appropriate. Plain text or regex parsing is less reliable.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Two evaluator agents rate the same generated architecture from 2/10 to 9/10 using the same rubric wording. What should improve score consistency?
options: Ask evaluators to use shorter explanations.
Use calibration examples for score levels.
Increase max_tokens for all evaluator runs.
Average all evaluator scores automatically.
questions.rationale: Rubrics need calibration examples that anchor score levels. Averaging inconsistent judgments hides the calibration problem instead of fixing it.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A tool schema requires a nested array of affected_services, and Claude often formats it incorrectly. Which addition is most useful?
options: A warning that malformed JSON fails.
A free-text services field instead.
input_examples showing valid nested arrays.
A second tool for each service entry.
questions.rationale: Concrete input examples help Claude format complex nested objects correctly. Flattening or tool proliferation sacrifices structure or increases tool-selection complexity.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 400-page contract fits in the context window. Claude must answer specific questions from it. What placement is generally recommended?
options: Use only a summary instead of the source contract.
Put questions first, then append the contract afterward.
Interleave each question after every contract section.
Put the long contract first and questions at the end.
questions.rationale: For long-context prompting, longform data should usually appear before the query. Summaries may lose details needed for precise answers.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: During compaction, exact claim IDs and promised refund amounts become vague. What should the system maintain?
options: A persistent structured facts block.
A longer compaction summary prompt.
A lower temperature during compaction.
A transcript link with no extracted facts.
questions.rationale: Critical identifiers, amounts, and commitments should be extracted into persistent structured state. Summaries alone can blur exact values.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A harness wants to inject fresh account status after server-side compaction but before conversation continues. Which configuration supports this pause?
options: A cache breakpoint on the latest user message.
pause_after_compaction returning a compaction stop.
A PostToolUse hook on the compaction block.
A larger max_tokens value for the next turn.
questions.rationale: pause_after_compaction lets the harness regain control after compaction and inject updated context. Cache breakpoints and output limits do not provide that pause.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A claims-extraction system reports 96% overall accuracy, but medical claims underperform on diagnosis_code. What evaluation method is missing?
options: A larger undifferentiated sample.
A lower global automation threshold.
Accuracy by document type and field.
Manual review of only failed claims.
questions.rationale: Aggregate accuracy can hide segment failures. Evaluation should be stratified by document type and field.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A form extractor outputs field confidence. The team wants one auto-approval threshold for all fields. Validation shows address fields are reliable at 0.85, while dates need 0.97. What should you do?
options: Use one conservative threshold for every extracted field.
Trust confidence only when Claude cites a snippet.
Ignore confidence and sample documents uniformly.
Calibrate thresholds per field with labeled data.
questions.rationale: Confidence should be calibrated with labeled validation data, often per field and document type. A global threshold wastes review on reliable fields and may under-review risky ones.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A high-volume review agent needs continuous quality monitoring without human review of every output. What evaluation architecture fits?
options: Use tiered evaluation with sampled semantic checks.
Manual review of every item before release.
Only aggregate monthly accuracy from approved cases.
Rely on model confidence to detect all risky outputs.
questions.rationale: Tiered evaluation combines cheap structural checks, sampled deeper evaluations, and targeted human review. It scales better than full manual review and is safer than confidence-only routing.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: Prompt cache hit rate drops after changing tool definitions, even though the system prompt is unchanged. What explains this?
options: Tools are never included in prompt-cache keys.
Tool definitions invalidate downstream cache layers.
Only user messages are eligible for caching.
The cache ignores requests containing tool_choice.
questions.rationale: Tool definitions sit high in the cache hierarchy. Changing them can invalidate cached system and message layers.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A team wants to test 80 mocked timeout and malformed-response cases overnight. The results are not blocking users. What is appropriate?
options: Wait for production incidents to occur.
Run every case manually in Claude Code.
Use Message Batches for offline evaluation.
Disable retries to expose failures faster.
questions.rationale: Message Batches are suitable for non-blocking bulk evaluation and edge-case testing. Manual or production-only testing is less scalable and less safe.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)

questions.text: A 3-hour codebase investigation keeps losing discovered file paths after compaction. The team wants state that survives context boundaries. What pattern should they use?
options: Use lower effort during exploration.
Increase max_tokens for every response.
Trust resumed chat history for memory.
Persist findings in a scratchpad file.
questions.rationale: Scratchpad files externalize investigation state so key paths, hypotheses, and findings can be re-read after compaction or a fresh start. Output token limits and effort settings do not preserve state.
questions.source: Rick Hightower — Intent Solutions CCA-F practice exams (reuse granted 2026-07-21)
